Arithmetic from the published L1/L2 total: the scratchpads total about 500 MB across the chip, so on the MiB reading, about 500 MB is 4,194,304,000 bits, about 25,165,824,000 6T cell transistors chip-wide, and on the decimal reading, 4,000,000,000 bits, 24,000,000,000 cell transistors — both readings are arithmetic on an approximate published total, so neither is an exact chip total. The per-tile L1 size and the per-cluster L2 size are not published, so no per-tile or per-cluster cell total is claimed, and the bank count, the bank width and the arbitration between the TTU, TVP and TDMA are not published, so the decoder, mux and sense-amplifier totals — which need the bank count — are not claimed. Standard construction.
- **DMA engine (the TDMA read/write copy engines)** — A DMA engine is address counters plus transfer control: in the standard form, a strided address generator is an address counter per dimension — an N-bit counter is N flip-flops plus N full adders, so a 16-bit counter is 768-896 transistors — plus the muxes selecting the stride per dimension (4 transistors per bit per 2:1 mux), under a small control FSM with state in master-slave D flip-flops. The TDMA fetches weight and activation tiles into L1 SRAM and writes finished tiles back out, in the sharding the compiler chose. The DMA channel count, the queue depths and the per-engine bandwidth are not published, so no DMA total is claimed — the 16-bit figure illustrates the per-bit counter form and is not a published width. Standard construction.
- **Mux / demux (operand steering — TTU, TVP and TDMA onto the L1 SRAM)** — A 2:1 mux is 4 transistors per bit in transmission-gate form, and selecting among R inputs is a mux tree of R-1 2:1 muxes per output bit — a 32:1 mux is 31 muxes in 5 levels, 124 transistors per bit. The three engines share the tile SRAM: the TDMA writes tiles in, the TTU reads operands out, the TVP reads and writes its post-op, and each selection is such a mux tree. The steering radices and widths are not published, so no mux total is claimed — the per-bit tree form is standard construction, not a published circuit. Standard construction.
- **Pipeline registers (the TTU/TVP pipeline stages)** — A pipeline stage boundary is a register: one D flip-flop per bit (about 20-28 transistors each) of the value crossing the boundary, clocked once per stage. The overlap model — the next tile is pulled in while the current GEMM runs, the TVP fuses the post-op while the TDMA fetches — implies staged execution with registers between stages. The stage counts and the register counts between stages are not published, so no pipeline total is claimed — the per-bit flip-flop cost is the only number this level can attach to the pipeline. Standard construction.
- **Compression datapath (the data compression engine)** — The deck names a data compression engine on the tile; it shrinks what must move and be stored, which is part of how the tile relieves the data-movement wall. The compression algorithm, the compression ratio and the engine's internals are not published, so no gate-level form is claimed for this engine: in the standard form a compression datapath is built from comparators, muxes and registers, but which of those, and in what arrangement, depends on the unpublished algorithm, so nothing more is stated here. Standard construction.
- **Credit counter — no hardware flow control published in the tile** — There is no published credit-based flow control in the tile: the flow control the published material describes is the hardware semaphores — a command waits on its in-semaphores and signals its out-semaphores. A credit counter in the standard form is a register plus decrement and increment logic — an N-bit counter is N D flip-flops plus N full adders — but no such counter is part of the published tile, so it is named here as absent from the published design, not as a primitive with unpublished parameters, and there is nothing to decompose and no credit-counter total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Data cache / tag array — none (no caches anywhere on Maia 100)** — The L1 and L2 scratchpads are software-managed, and every byte the tile touches arrived by an explicit DMA — there is no tag array, no replacement logic and no coherence hardware on the tile path. A tag array in the standard form is a CAM — a CAM cell is an SRAM cell plus XOR match logic feeding a matchline, about 10 transistors per cell — with one XOR comparison per tag bit and an AND tree over the matchline, but no such structure exists on the tile path, so there is nothing to decompose and no tag total is claimed. Standard construction.

Parameter honesty: the published tile geometry used above — five pieces around a tile SRAM, the TTU's 16xRx16 shape, MX blocks of 32 elements sharing one 8-bit E8M0 scale, a loosely coupled superscalar vector processor with a custom ISA for FP32 and BF16, a DMA engine supporting different tensor sharding schemes, hardware semaphores, and software-managed L1/L2 scratchpads totalling about 500 MB — and the arithmetic is derived from those published counts. Below that level — TTU multiplier staging and accumulator widths, TVP register counts and lane counts, L1 bank organisation, command-queue depths, DMA channel counts, compression-engine internals — Microsoft publishes nothing, and this decomposition invents nothing. Two things are absent by design and are stated as such: there is no data cache and no tag array anywhere on the tile, because the scratchpads are software-managed and every byte arrives by explicit DMA; and there is no published credit-based flow control in the tile, because the hardware semaphores are the flow control.

#### Down to the gates: The cluster, the mesh NoC and the gather-based distributed GEMM

Microsoft publishes no gate-level structure for the cluster, the mesh NoC or the gather path either — the Hot Chips 2024 deck describes the complex's contract (16 clusters of four tiles on a mesh-like high-bandwidth data mesh NoC, a Cluster NOC, CCP and CDMA plus L2 SRAM per cluster, 64 GB of HBM2E at 1.8 TB/s behind a 4096-IO PHY, a PAM4 112G SerDes PHY driving 12x 400 GbE backend links, up to 4800 Gbps all-gather and scatter-reduce and 1200 Gbps all-to-all, a 32 GB/s PCIe host link, and a custom RoCE-like Ethernet protocol with AES-GCM encryption) and stops there. The same gate-term search this run found no transistor, flip-flop, latch or NAND content in the deck, the Tech Community writeup or the Azure blog. What follows takes each Level-3 primitive down to gates and transistors on the same terms as the tile block: published geometry stays published, arithmetic is labelled as arithmetic, and every gate form is the textbook-standard construction, labelled as such.

- **Crossbar (the Cluster NOC — switching four tiles, the CCP and the CDMA)** — A crossbar is a mux tree per output: in the standard form, an output selecting among R inputs is R-1 2:1 muxes per output bit (4 transistors per mux in transmission-gate form), so a 32-bit output selecting among R sources is 32 x (R-1) muxes, with the select bits held in configuration flip-flops (20-28 transistors each). The cluster's pieces connect through the Cluster NOC, switching the four tiles' requests and the CDMA's traffic onto the cluster SRAM and the mesh. The crossbar's port counts, radix and per-port widths are not published, so no crossbar total is claimed — the mux-tree form is standard construction, not a published circuit. Standard construction.
- **Switch arbiter (mesh router arbitration across 16 clusters)** — An arbiter is a priority encoder plus grant state: in the standard form, one AND gate per requester fed by the request bits, a grant flip-flop per output port (20-28 transistors each) holding the winner until the access clears, and the encoder tree that picks the highest-priority pending request. Sixteen clusters sit on a mesh-like high-bandwidth data mesh NoC, the diagram showing the clusters in a grid with routers at the intersections, so each router arbitrates the clusters' traffic onto its links. The arbiters' structure, port counts and fairness policy are not published, so no arbiter total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **FIFO / queue (mesh router buffers and the cluster command queues)** — A FIFO is a storage array plus two pointer counters plus full/empty comparators: as registers, N entries of W bits is N x W D flip-flops (N x W x 20-28 transistors); the write and read pointers are counters (an N-bit pointer counter is N flip-flops plus N full adders); full and empty are comparators of the two pointers (one XOR gate per pointer bit plus an AND tree over the bits). Requests wait in the network between issue and service — the CCP issues cluster commands, the CDMA moves tiles, the routers forward them — so each stage holds requests in queues. The queue depths, the packet format and the per-stage buffering are not published, so no queue total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **SRAM bank (the cluster SRAM / L2 — CSRAM)** — The cluster SRAM is an array of 6T SRAM cells in the primer's SRAM bank form — each stored bit is 6 transistors (two cross-coupled inverters, 4 transistors, plus two access transistors), plus the per-bank row decoder, column muxes and sense amplifiers. The per-cluster SRAM size is not published — only the about 500 MB L1/L2 total — so no CSRAM cell total is claimed here; the chip-wide approximate cell total from that total is stated in the tile block and is not repeated, so the two blocks never double-count it. The bank count, bank width and arbitration inside a cluster are not published, so the decoder, mux and sense-amplifier totals — which need the bank count — are not claimed. Standard construction.
- **DMA engine (the CDMA — cluster DMA)** — A DMA engine is address counters plus transfer control: in the standard form, a strided address generator is an address counter per dimension — an N-bit counter is N flip-flops plus N full adders, so a 16-bit counter is 768-896 transistors — plus the muxes selecting the stride per dimension (4 transistors per bit per 2:1 mux), under a small control FSM with state in master-slave D flip-flops. The deck names a CDMA per cluster; it moves tiles between the cluster SRAM, the mesh and HBM. The DMA channel count, the queue depths and the per-engine bandwidth are not published, so no DMA total is claimed — the 16-bit figure illustrates the per-bit counter form and is not a published width. Standard construction.
- **FSM / controller (the Cluster Control Processor — cluster command issue)** — The CCP is a control FSM: in the standard form, the control state lives in master-slave D flip-flops (about 20-28 transistors each) with next-state logic as a NAND/NOR network, and the issue logic dispatches commands to the cluster's engines. The deck names a CCP per cluster; it issues commands to the cluster's engines, the cluster-level counterpart of the tile's TCP. Its issue policy and its own pipeline structure are not published, so no state-bit count and no controller total is claimed — the FSM form is standard construction, not a published circuit. Standard construction.
- **Mux / demux (HBM2E PHY data muxing — 4096 IO onto four HBM2E stacks)** — A 2:1 mux is 4 transistors per bit in transmission-gate form, and selecting among R inputs is a mux tree of R-1 2:1 muxes per output bit. The HBM2E PHY carries 4096 IO feeding four HBM2E stacks, 64 GB at 1.8 TB/s — 16 GB and 1,024 IO per stack by arithmetic — and selecting among four stacks needs 2 address bits by arithmetic. The PHY's mux structure and the per-stack channel organisation are not published, so no mux total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **SerDes (the PAM4 112G PHY — 12x 400 GbE backend links)** — A serializer is a mux tree plus flip-flops: in the standard form, parallel-to-serial conversion selects one bit per cycle out of the parallel word through a mux tree (R-1 2:1 muxes per output bit, 4 transistors per mux in transmission-gate form), clocked out of a register, and a deserializer is the reverse — a serial bit shifted into a register one cycle at a time. The backend runs 12x 400 GbE — 4,800 Gbps, 600 GB/s by arithmetic — over a PAM4 112G SerDes PHY. The equalizer structure, the clock-and-data-recovery detail and the per-lane organisation are not published, so no SerDes total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Crypto engine (AES-GCM on the custom RoCE-like backend)** — An AES round in the standard form is four steps: SubBytes, an S-box substitution per byte; ShiftRows, a rewiring of the byte positions; MixColumns, an XOR tree over Galois-field arithmetic; and AddRoundKey, one XOR gate per bit (10-12 transistors each) against the round key. GCM adds GHASH, a Galois-field multiplier over the ciphertext, and counter mode, a counter plus one XOR per bit against the keystream. The backend network runs a custom RoCE-like Ethernet protocol with AES-GCM encryption, on a unified backend network serving both scale-up and scale-out. The key widths, the encryption throughput and the engine's pipeline are not published, so no crypto total is claimed — the S-box form and the GHASH multiplier width are not published either, so no count is attached to them. Standard construction.
- **Adder tree (the gather GEMM's final sum — Y0 = Y00+Y01+Y02+Y03 plus bias)** — The deck's worked example is a 2048 (M) x 12288 (K) x 12288 (N) GEMM split across 4 chips, K/4 per chip, and the output stage sums all four partials — Y0 = Y00 + Y01 + Y02 + Y03 — plus the bias, all in SRAM. The output has 2048 x 12288 = 25,165,824 elements by arithmetic, each needing four adds plus the bias add, and each add in the standard form is a full-adder chain, one full adder per bit at 28 transistors per bit. The adder widths and the precision of the final sum are not published, so no sum total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Address generator (the gather addressing — K/4 partition, per-chip slice selection)** — An address generator in the standard form is counters plus adders: an N-bit address counter is N D flip-flops plus N full adders, so a 16-bit counter is 768-896 transistors, and a strided address is a base plus a counter times a stride, one adder per address bit. The gather fetches the pieces each chip needs by address: the input cut K/4 so each chip owns one K-slice — K = 12288, so K/4 = 3,072 per chip by arithmetic — and the weights staged as W00 through W33 across the four chips. The address-generator structure and the gather's request format are not published, so no address-generator total is claimed — the 16-bit figure illustrates the per-bit counter form and is not a published width. Standard construction.
- **Credit counter — no flow-control scheme published for the mesh** — The published material describes no credit-based flow control for the mesh NoC: no credit counters, no backpressure scheme and no published buffer accounting between the routers. A credit counter in the standard form is a register plus decrement and increment logic — an N-bit counter is N D flip-flops plus N full adders — but no such counter is part of the published design, so it is named here as absent from the published design, not as a primitive with unpublished parameters, and there is nothing to decompose and no credit-counter total is claimed. Flow control, as far as the published material goes, is the semaphore/command model inside the tiles and the gather scheduling across chips. Standard construction.
- **Synchronizer (the SerDes/PCIe clock-domain crossings)** — A synchronizer is two flip-flops in series per crossing bit: in the standard 2-flop form, one D flip-flop (about 20-28 transistors) in the source clock domain feeding a second D flip-flop (about 20-28 transistors) in the destination domain, 40-56 transistors per synchronised bit, so a metastable first flop settles before the second samples it. The PAM4 112G SerDes PHY and the PCIe PHY are clock-domain crossings by construction — the backend and host links run on their own clocks against the on-die mesh. The synchronizer structure, the SerDes clocking and the PCIe lane organisation are not published, so no synchronizer total beyond the per-bit cost is claimed. Standard construction.

Parameter honesty: the published complex geometry used above — 16 clusters of four tiles, a mesh-like high-bandwidth data mesh NoC, a Cluster NOC, CCP and CDMA plus L2 SRAM per cluster, 64 GB of HBM2E at 1.8 TB/s behind a 4096-IO PHY, a PAM4 112G SerDes PHY driving 12x 400 GbE backend links, up to 4800 Gbps all-gather/scatter-reduce and 1200 Gbps all-to-all, a 32 GB/s PCIe host link, and a custom RoCE-like Ethernet protocol with AES-GCM encryption — and the arithmetic is derived from those published counts. Below that level — NoC radix, link widths and buffer depths, cluster-SRAM bank organisation, CDMA channel counts, SerDes equalizer and CDR detail, AES-GCM key and throughput figures, synchronizer structure — Microsoft publishes nothing, and this decomposition invents nothing. Two things are absent by design and are stated as such: there is no HBM on the gather path, because network reads and writes are served directly from cluster SRAM; and no flow-control scheme is published for the mesh, because the published flow control lives in the semaphore/command model and the gather scheduling. The cluster-level connection engine is named on the deck's async-programming slide but its internal function is not detailed, so it is named here and not decomposed.

### AMD VCN 4.0 / Media Engine

**Specs (wiki card).** RDNA 3 MCD-adjacent media block · AV1 encode/decode

**Building blocks.**
- **Unified codec core** — One block succeeding AMD's separate UVD decoder and VCE encoder lineages: H.264, HEVC encode/decode, VP9 and AV1 decode in a single engine that shares its front-end across standards
- **AV1 encode unit ★** — VCN 4.0's headline addition — hardware AV1 encoding (8/10-bit) alongside AV1 decode, the feature that put RDNA 3 at parity with NVENC and Quick Sync for streamers
- **Dual media engines (Navi 31 class)** — High-end RDNA 3 parts carry two VCN instances so two encode sessions (or one very fast one) proceed in parallel; smaller APUs carry one
- **JPEG / picture engine** — Still-image decode acceleration sharing the block — the unglamorous path every photo viewer and browser exercises
- **AMF runtime interface** — The Advanced Media Framework API and driver layer that exposes the block to FFmpeg and OBS — the software surface that decides whether the silicon is actually used
- **Display-adjacent power states** — Aggressive clock/power gating so video playback runs on the media block alone at milliwatts — the laptop-battery feature, not the headline one

**The piece that makes it special.** Unification completed, then AV1. VCN's architectural story is convergence: decode (UVD) and encode (VCE) grew up as separate blocks with separate bugs; VCN merged them into one engine whose per-generation delta is a codec checklist. VCN 4.0's checklist item — AV1 encode — mattered out of proportion to its area because it removed the last reason creator workloads defaulted to a rival's GPU. Note the honesty limit: AMD publishes VCN's codec/rate support, not an internal block diagram — the stages inside the core are not publicly documented, and this entry does not invent them.

#### Inside the signature block: The dual media engines and the AV1 encode path — two whole encoders, one new codec

**Inside it.** Navi 31- and Navi 32-class parts carry two VCN 4.0 instances on the graphics compute die; Navi 33-class parts carry one — AMD's ROCm decode table lists two VCNs for gfx1100 and gfx1102 and one for gfx1101. Each instance is a complete unified codec engine, encoding and decoding H.264, HEVC, VP9 and AV1, not a helper stage bolted onto a bigger block. The generation's new codec is AV1: hardware AV1 encoding (8/10-bit, 4:2:0) alongside AV1 decode, the feature that put RDNA 3 at parity with NVENC and Quick Sync for streamers. AMD's press release frames the pair as simultaneous encode or decode streams up to 8K60 for HEVC with AV1 encode, at up to 1.8X the engine frequency of RDNA 2, and claims AV1 hardware encoding up to 7X faster at 8K than a software-only solution. Two software-visible additions ride on the encode path. First, the media engine integrates Xilinx content-adaptive machine learning technology, per AMD's own release, to enhance text quality at lower resolutions and bitrates — the Xilinx acquisition's fingerprint on the encode pipeline. Second, AMF pre-analysis sits in front of the encoder: it computes a per-block content-activity metric plus scene-change and static-scene flags, and the encoder uses those results for adaptive quantization, forced intra frames on scene changes and skip frames on static scenes; its lookahead buffer runs 0 to 41 frames, and AMD's programming guide states the trade plainly — the longer the buffer, the better the quality and the longer the latency. The encode itself follows the codec-mandated AV1 pipeline: superblocks partition from 128x128 down to 4x4, motion is estimated against up to seven reference frames, and symbols are packed by AV1's CDF-based multi-symbol arithmetic coder — not CABAC, which AV1 does not use. AMD publishes no internal sub-block diagram for VCN — no stage latencies, queue depths, reference-store sizes or buffer geometry — so this block describes the published pipeline stages and the API-visible contract, and invents no circuits inside them.

**Trace — one unit of work: one 4K60 AV1 frame through one VCN encode engine.**
1. **Frame arrives from VRAM. **A rendered or captured 4K frame is handed to the encode session from GPU memory; the shader cores and CPU are already free, because the frame's encode will not touch them.
2. **Pre-analysis reads the frame first. **The AMF pre-analysis component inspects the frame before encoding, scoring content activity block by block and flagging scene changes and static scenes; the encoder will spend bits where pre-analysis says the content is, and skip frames where it says nothing moved.
3. **Motion estimation and mode decision. **The engine searches motion against up to seven AV1 reference frames and chooses intra or inter prediction per block, partitioning superblocks from 128x128 down to 4x4 — the most expensive stage of the pipeline, and the one the lookahead buffer feeds.
4. **Compensation, transform, quantise. **Motion compensation forms the residual, which is transformed and quantised under adaptive quantization driven by the pre-analysis results — the preset and rate-control mode that decide the quality-versus-speed trade.
5. **Entropy coding. **AV1's CDF-based multi-symbol arithmetic coder packs the quantised residuals and mode data into the bitstream; H.264 and HEVC sessions take the CABAC path in the same engine instead. Xilinx content-adaptive machine-learning tuning shapes the low-bitrate result.
6. **Bitstream out; second engine takes the next session. **The bitstream returns to memory for OBS, FFmpeg or the application; the second VCN instance on Navi 31- and Navi 32-class parts encodes the next stream in parallel, since there is no driver lock on encode sessions — while a single session's rate stays one engine's rate.

**Bottleneck in / out.** Relieves the creator-parity gap: before VCN 4.0, streaming on a Radeon meant the H.264 encoder reviewers measured as behind NVENC and Quick Sync, or a CPU encode; with hardware AV1 encode plus no session lock, the card records, streams and archives at once while the shaders keep gaming. Creates a single-engine ceiling instead: one 4K60 AV1 encode at the High Quality preset pegs the encoder hardware at 100 percent usage, so a second session shares the engine rather than getting a free one, and the second VCN instance only helps a single stream when the work is split across sessions. The codec menu is fixed at tape-out — VCN 4.0 has no VVC path — and AV1 encode carries a hardware quirk: Navi 3.x's AV1 encoder requires resolutions divisible by 64 in both dimensions, so exact 1080p is padded internally and cropped back. Quality still trails the rivals on the legacy codecs: H.264 encoding improved over RDNA 2 but still lags NVIDIA and Intel in reviewers' tests, and the quality jump is bought with lookahead latency — the pre-analysis buffer that sharpens high-motion scenes is the same buffer that delays the stream.

**Governing numbers.** 2 VCN 4.0 instances on Navi 31- and Navi 32-class parts (gfx1100, gfx1102); 1 on Navi 33-class parts (gfx1101); AV1 encode/decode 8/10-bit, 4:2:0; HEVC/H.264 encode/decode; VP9 decode; JPEG decode; encode rates (AMD reviewer's guide, via PCWorld): 4K up to 180 fps H.264/HEVC, 240 fps AV1; 8K 48 fps HEVC, 60 fps AV1; 1080p/1440p 360 fps in all three codecs; simultaneous encode/decode streams up to 8K60 for HEVC; engine frequency up to 1.8X RDNA 2; AV1 hardware encode up to 7X faster at 8K than software-only (AMD); no driver lock on encode sessions (NVIDIA GeForce is limited to 3); pre-analysis lookahead buffer 0–41 frames; Phoenix APUs: AV1 encode up to 4K240 10-bit; AV1 partitions 128x128 down to 4x4; up to 7 AV1 reference frames. Internal stage latencies, queue depths and buffer sizes: not published.

**Primary source.** AMD, 'AMD Unveils World's Most Advanced Gaming Graphics Cards, Built on Groundbreaking AMD RDNA 3 Architecture with Chiplet Design' (press release, November 3, 2022) — Dual Media Engine and New AMD RDNA 3 Media Engine sections; AMD ROCm, 'rocDecode supported codecs and hardware capabilities' (2026-11-18) — VCN generation and instance table; AMD GPUOpen AMF, 'Advanced Media Framework – Pre-Analysis Component Programming Guide' — §§1.2, 2, LOOKAHEAD_BUFFER_DEPTH; PCWorld, Taylor, 'Tested: With RDNA 3, AMD Radeon is finally useful for content creators' (December 14, 2022) — AMD reviewer's-guide encode rates and no-driver-lock sessions; TechPowerUp, 'AMD Ryzen 7040 Series Phoenix Point Mobile Processor I/O Detailed' — Phoenix VCN AV1 encode rate; AOMedia, 'AV1 Bitstream & Decoding Process Specification' v1.0.0 with Errata 1 — §8.3 (CDF symbol decoding), §3 (CDEF, loop filter); libaom, 'AV1 Encoder Guide' — block partitions, in-loop filters; HandBrake, 'AMD VCN' documentation — Known Limitations (AV1 resolution rule).
#### Inside the signature block: The decode pipeline — one unified core, bounded by the codec table

**Inside it.** Decode is not a separate engine from encode in VCN — the same unified core that encodes also decodes, which is the whole point of the VCN unification: UVD and VCE were separate blocks, VCN is one. AMD's ROCm decode table is the contract: on Navi 3x, VCN 4.0 decodes HEVC 8/10-bit to 7680x4320, VP9 8/10-bit to 7680x4320, AV1 8/10-bit to 8192x4352, and H.264 8-bit to 4096x2176 — and that H.264 cap is the tell: the oldest codec in the core is the one that stops at 4K while the newer codecs run to 8K, so an 8K H.264 stream is not a decode job for this block at all. The decode pipeline itself is the codec-mandated inverse of encode: the CDF symbol decoder unpacks the bitstream, inverse transforms and prediction reconstruct each block against its reference frames, and the in-loop filters — deblocking, then AV1's constrained directional enhancement filter (CDEF), then loop restoration — clean the reconstruction before it is stored as a reference for the frames that follow. The same core also decodes JPEG stills, the path every photo viewer and browser exercises, and the decoded frame can feed the display engine directly. Decode runs concurrently with encode — AMD's dual-media-engine claim is simultaneous encode or decode streams — and independently of the shader cores, so playback costs the game nothing. As with encode, AMD publishes no internal sub-block diagram for the decode path — no entropy-decoder, inverse-transform or reference-store internals — so this block describes the published contract and the codec-mandated stages, not invented circuits.

**Trace — one unit of work: one AV1 frame through the decoder.**
1. **Bitstream arrives. **An AV1 bitstream is handed to a decode session on one VCN instance; the driver queues it through AMF or the video acceleration API, and the shader cores are not involved.
2. **Entropy decode. **The CDF symbol decoder unpacks mode data, motion vectors and quantised coefficients from the bitstream — the inverse of the encode's arithmetic coding, driven by the same cumulative-distribution tables.
3. **Reconstruction. **Inverse transforms and prediction rebuild each block — superblocks partitioned 128x128 down to 4x4 — against up to seven reference frames held from earlier decoded frames.
4. **In-loop filtering. **Deblocking smooths block edges, CDEF filters adaptively along detected directions, and loop restoration (Wiener or self-guided, per 64x64 to 256x256 unit) finishes the reconstruction.
5. **Reference store in video memory. **The finished frame is written to VRAM as a reference for the frames that follow it; the application never stages it through the CPU.
6. **Frame out, in parallel with everything else. **The decoded frame goes to the display engine or to a consumer, while the other VCN instance encodes another stream and the shaders keep rendering — three tenants on one die, no interference.

**Bottleneck in / out.** Relieves the decode tax the same way the encode path relieves encode: video playback and transcoding stop competing with the game or the training job for shader cores and CPU cores, and the faster-than-real-time rates make VCN a transcoding engine, not just a player. Creates a codec-table ceiling instead: the decode maxima are per codec, not per engine — H.264 stops at 4096x2176 while AV1 runs to 8192x4352, so the oldest standard is the bottleneck for legacy 8K content, and the codec menu is fixed like encode's, with no VVC decode. And because decode shares the unified core with encode, a heavy encode and a heavy decode on the same single-VCN part share the one engine — the dual-instance parts are the ones where decode and encode truly run side by side.

**Governing numbers.** Decode maxima (AMD ROCm rocDecode docs, VCN 4.0 Navi 3x): AV1 8192x4352 (8/10-bit); HEVC 7680x4320 (8/10-bit); VP9 7680x4320 (8/10-bit); H.264 4096x2176 (8-bit only); JPEG decode; 2 VCN instances on gfx1100/gfx1102, 1 on gfx1101; simultaneous encode/decode streams up to 8K60 for HEVC (AMD press release); AV1 in-loop filters: deblocking, CDEF, loop restoration on 64x64/128x128/256x256 units; AV1 partitions 128x128 down to 4x4. Internal stage breakdown: not published.

**Primary source.** AMD ROCm, 'rocDecode supported codecs and hardware capabilities' (2026-11-18) — VCN generation and instance table; AMD, 'AMD Unveils World's Most Advanced Gaming Graphics Cards, Built on Groundbreaking AMD RDNA 3 Architecture with Chiplet Design' (press release, November 3, 2022) — Dual Media Engine section; AOMedia, 'AV1 Bitstream & Decoding Process Specification' v1.0.0 with Errata 1 — §3 (CDEF, loop filter), §8.3 (CDF symbol decoding); libaom, 'AV1 Encoder Guide' — block partitions, post-encode loop filtering.

#### Down to the primitives: The dual media engines and the AV1 encode path — two whole encoders, one new codec

The two VCN 4.0 instances run the published encode pipeline — pre-analysis, motion estimation and mode decision, motion compensation and residual coding, entropy coding — and each stage is built from the primitives below. Numbers that come from a codec specification are spec facts about the algorithm, not published facts about AMD's silicon; where a primitive's geometry is not published, that is stated plainly.

- **SRAM bank (reference frame store)** — The motion estimator searches against up to seven AV1 reference frames (verified — already recorded at Level 2), so each engine must hold several decoded frames on chip while it searches them. That store is an SRAM bank — or a set of banks, one per reference — written by the reconstruction loop and read by the motion estimator and the motion compensator. Its capacity in frames, its banking and its port count are not published. Standard construction for the store itself; the seven-reference-frame figure is a published contract, not a bank size.
- **FIFO / queue (frame ingest and dual-engine handoff)** — Frames arrive from VRAM and are queued to an encode session; the second VCN instance on Navi 31- and Navi 32-class parts takes the next session in parallel, since there is no driver lock on encode sessions (verified — already recorded at Level 2). The ingest queue and the dual-engine handoff are FIFOs decoupling the frame source from the two engines. Their depths and widths are not published.
- **Adder tree + comparator (motion-estimation SAD and best-match selection)** — Motion estimation scores each candidate displacement by a sum of absolute differences: per-pixel subtractors feeding an adder tree, with a comparator keeping the lowest-cost candidate as the search proceeds. The search is the most expensive stage of the pipeline (verified — already recorded at Level 2: the Level-2 trace names motion estimation and mode decision as the most expensive stage). The candidate set, the search range, the block sizes the search covers and the SAD datapath width are not published. Standard construction for the SAD arithmetic.
- **Multiplier array (motion-compensation 8-tap interpolation)** — Sub-pixel motion compensation interpolates reference samples with the codec's filters, and AV1's are 8-tap: the spec names EIGHTTAP, EIGHTTAP_SMOOTH and EIGHTTAP_SHARP, and its inter-prediction process sums eight filter taps per sample (verified — AV1 Bitstream & Decoding Process Specification v1.0.0 with Errata 1, §7.11.3 inter prediction; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). Each tap is a multiply, so the interpolator is a multiplier array feeding an adder tree. This is a spec fact about the algorithm the silicon must implement, not a published fact about VCN's interpolator geometry — the array's width and tap parallelism are not published.
- **Adder tree + multiplier array (transform butterflies and quantisation)** — The residual is transformed and quantised. AV1's transform stage is four separable 1-D transforms — DCT, ADST, flipped ADST and identity — combinable into 16 2-D kernels, applied at 19 scales from 64x64 down to 4x4 (verified — libaom AV1 Encoder Guide: "AV1 implements the transform stage using 4 seperable 1-d transforms (DCT, ADST, FLIPADST and IDTX, where FLIPADST is the reversed version of ADST and IDTX is the identity transform) which can be combined to give 16 2-d combinations" and "These combinations can be applied at 19 different scales from 64x64 pixels down to 4x4 pixels"; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). A butterfly stage is an adder tree with coefficient multipliers; quantisation is a further multiply by the reciprocal step. Spec facts about the transform set; the butterfly depth, the multiplier count and the quantiser datapath are not published.
- **Register file (CDF probability tables and CABAC context models)** — The entropy stage keeps its probability state in tables. For AV1 the spec defines the CDF as "Cumulative distribution function representing the probability times 32768 that a symbol has value less than or equal to a given level" (verified — AV1 spec, §3 Terms and definitions; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3), with the top entry equal to 1 << 15 (verified — AV1 spec, §8.3 Symbol decoding process; already recorded at Level 2), and the last CDF entry counting decoded symbols up to a maximum of 32 so the adaptation rate depends on it (verified — AV1 spec, §8.3; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). For H.264/HEVC the CABAC context models are a 127-state finite-state estimator per model, with probabilities in [0.01875, 0.98125] (verified — Fraunhofer HHI, CABAC: "Each probability model in CABAC can take one out of 127 different states with associated probability values p ranging in the interval [0.01875, 0,98125]"; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). The tables are a register file (or small SRAM) indexed by syntax element and context; the table count, entry count and banking are not published. Spec facts about the tables; nothing about VCN's table storage is published.
- **FSM / controller (the arithmetic coder state machine)** — AV1's entropy coder is an M-ary symbol arithmetic coder — "In contrast, AV1 uses an M-ary symbol arithmetic coder to compress the syntax elements, where integer M∈[2, 14]" (verified — libaom AV1 Encoder Guide; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3) — and the spec's symbol decoding process is a range/value state machine with renormalisation after every symbol (verified — AV1 spec, §8.3; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). The coder's control is an FSM stepping through range subdivision, renormalisation and CDF update, while CABAC's binary M-coder runs the same shape of loop one bin at a time (verified — Fraunhofer HHI: "The design of CABAC involves the key elements of binarization, context modeling, and binary arithmetic coding"; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). The FSM's state count and the coder's symbol-per-clock rate are not published.
- **Barrel shifter (range renormalisation and bitstream packing)** — After each symbol the arithmetic coder renormalises: the spec sets bits = 15 − FloorLog2(SymbolRange) and shifts SymbolRange left by that amount (verified — AV1 spec, §8.3 Symbol decoding process; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3), and the emitted bits are packed into the output stream. That variable shift is a barrel shifter, and the bitstream packer is a second one. The shift width and the packer's buffer depth are not published. Standard construction for the shifter; the renormalisation rule is a spec fact.
- **Comparator (mode decision — best prediction mode)** — Mode decision chooses intra or inter prediction per block — the stage the Level-2 trace names alongside motion estimation — by comparing the rate-distortion cost of the candidate modes and keeping the cheapest. AV1's mode space is large: 71 basic intra prediction modes and 56 single-frame inter prediction modes, plus compound modes (verified — libaom AV1 Encoder Guide: "AV1 also provides 71 basic intra prediction modes, 56 single frame inter prediction modes (7 reference frames x 4 modes x 2 for OBMC (overlapped block motion compensation)), 12768 compound inter prediction modes (that combine inter predictors from two reference frames) and 36708 compound inter / intra prediction modes"; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3), over block partitions from 128x128 pixels down to 4x4 using a multi-layer recursive tree structure (verified — libaom AV1 Encoder Guide: "AV1 supports block partitions of various sizes from 128x128 pixels down to 4x4 pixels using a multi-layer recursive tree structure"; already recorded at Level 2). The cost comparison is a comparator tree; the cost metric, the candidate pruning and the comparator width are not published. Spec facts about the mode counts and partitions; the decision circuit is standard construction.
- **Priority encoder (transform-coefficient scan and end-of-block)** — Coefficient coding walks the block's coefficients in the spec's scan order and signals the end of block — the position of the last non-zero coefficient — before coding levels in reverse scan order (verified — libaom AV1 Encoder Guide: "The encoder will code transform block skip flag (txb_skip). If the skip flag is off, then the encoder will code the end of block position (eob) which is the scan index of the last non-zero coefficient plus one"; new fact record this run). Finding the last non-zero coefficient in a coefficient vector is a priority-encoder operation. The scan tables are spec facts; the encoder's coefficient datapath width and the priority encoder's size are not published.
- **Counter (rate-control budget and CDF update count)** — Rate control — the preset and rate-control mode that decide the quality-versus-speed trade (verified — already recorded at Level 2) — tracks bits spent against the frame budget with counters, and the CDF update count is itself a counter the spec bounds: "The last entry of the cdf array is used to keep a count of the number of times the symbol has been decoded (up to a maximum of 32). This allows the cdf adaption rate to depend on the number of times the symbol has been decoded." (verified — AV1 spec, §8.3; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). The 32 cap is a spec fact; the rate-control counters' widths and the budget arithmetic are not published.
- **Mux / demux (session steering across the two VCN instances)** — The driver steers encode sessions to the available VCN instance with no driver lock and no application code (verified — already recorded at Level 2), and on Navi 31- and Navi 32-class parts the second instance takes the next session in parallel (verified — already recorded at Level 2). Both are mux/demux operations: sessions steered to instance 0 or 1, and the two bitstreams steered back to their callers. The steering fabric's radix, widths and arbitration are not published.
- **Accumulator array (pre-analysis content-activity metrics)** — Before encoding, AMF pre-analysis scores content activity block by block and flags scene changes and static scenes, and the encoder uses those results for adaptive quantization, forced intra frames on scene changes and skip frames on static scenes (verified — AMD GPUOpen AMF Pre-Analysis Programming Guide; already recorded at Level 2). The per-block activity scores are accumulated in registers — one accumulator per block, summed over the block's pixels — and the lookahead buffer holds 0 to 41 frames of them (verified — already recorded at Level 2). The accumulator widths, the block grid the metric is computed over and the lookahead buffer's storage form are not published. The Xilinx content-adaptive machine-learning tuning that shapes the low-bitrate result is likewise a published integration, not a published circuit.

**Parameter honesty.** Parameter honesty: the published encode-pipeline facts are the AMD contract (two VCN 4.0 instances on Navi 31/32-class parts, one on Navi 33; simultaneous encode or decode streams up to 8K60 for HEVC; AV1 hardware encode; Xilinx content-adaptive machine learning; AMF pre-analysis with per-block content-activity metric, scene-change and static-scene flags and a 0–41 frame lookahead; encode rates 4K 180 fps H.264/HEVC and 240 fps AV1, 8K 48 fps HEVC and 60 fps AV1; no driver lock on encode sessions; AV1 encode resolution divisible by 64 in both dimensions; Phoenix AV1 encode up to 4K240 10-bit) and the codec-spec facts (AV1 M-ary arithmetic coder with M in [2, 14]; CDF probability times 32768 with top entry 1 << 15 and update count capped at 32; 15-bit probability model with only the top 9 bits used by the encoder; 4 1-D transforms into 16 2-D kernels at 19 scales from 64x64 to 4x4; 71 intra and 56 single-frame inter modes over 128x128-to-4x4 partitions; 8-tap interpolation filters; transform-block skip flag and end-of-block as the scan index of the last non-zero coefficient plus one; CABAC binarization plus context modeling plus binary arithmetic coding with 127-state probability models). Below that level — reference-store capacity and banking, FIFO depths, SAD search range and datapath width, interpolator array width, butterfly depth and multiplier count, CDF/CABAC table counts and banking, coder FSM state count and symbol rate, renormalisation shift width, mode-decision cost metric, coefficient datapath width, rate-control counter widths, steering-fabric radix, pre-analysis accumulator widths and lookahead-buffer storage — AMD publishes nothing, and this decomposition invents nothing.

#### Down to the primitives: The decode pipeline — one unified core, bounded by the codec table

Decode is the inverse of the encode loop, carried out entirely in the fixed-function block — entropy decode, reconstruction against reference frames, in-loop filtering, and the frame's handoff to display or memory. As with encode, AMD publishes no internals, so the primitives below are mapped from the published contract and the codec specifications.

- **SRAM bank (reference frame store and decoded-frame buffer)** — Decoded frames stay available as references for the frames that follow them, and AV1 can reference up to seven of them (verified — AV1 spec, §3 constants: REFS_PER_FRAME 7, "Number of reference frames that can be used for inter prediction"; the seven-reference figure is already recorded at Level 2). The store is an SRAM bank (or banks) written by the reconstruction loop and read by motion compensation and the in-loop filters. Its capacity, banking and port count are not published.
- **FIFO / queue (bitstream ingest and session queueing)** — Bitstreams are handed to a decode session on one VCN instance and queued through AMF or the video acceleration API (verified — already recorded at Level 2: the Level-2 trace), and decode runs concurrently with encode on the same die (verified — already recorded at Level 2). The bitstream ingest path and the per-session state are queued through FIFOs. Queue depths, session-store size and the queueing mechanism are not published.
- **Register file (CDF tables and CABAC context state, per session)** — Each decode session carries its own probability state: AV1 CDF tables — probability times 32768, top entry 1 << 15, update count capped at 32 (verified — AV1 spec, §3 and §8.3; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3 and at Level 2 for VCN) — and CABAC's 127-state context models (verified — Fraunhofer HHI: "Each probability model in CABAC can take one out of 127 different states with associated probability values p ranging in the interval [0.01875, 0,98125]"; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). The tables are a register file indexed by syntax element and context, one copy per active session. The table count and the per-session storage size are not published. Spec facts about the tables; nothing about VCN's storage is published.
- **FSM / controller (the symbol decoder state machine)** — The spec's symbol decoding process is a state machine: "The input to this process is an array cdf of length N + 1 which specifies the cumulative distribution for a symbol with N possible values. The output of this process is the variable symbol, containing a decoded syntax element. The process also modifies the input array cdf to adapt the probabilities to the content of the stream." (verified — AV1 spec, §8.3; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). The decoder's control FSM steps through range subdivision, renormalisation and CDF update for every symbol; CABAC's binary decoding loop is the same shape (verified — Fraunhofer HHI: "The design of CABAC involves the key elements of binarization, context modeling, and binary arithmetic coding"; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). The FSM's state count and symbols-per-clock rate are not published.
- **Barrel shifter (renormalisation and literal bit reads)** — The symbol decoder renormalises after every symbol — bits = 15 − FloorLog2(SymbolRange), SymbolRange shifted left by that amount (verified — AV1 spec, §8.3; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3) — and literal/uncompressed header values are read straight from the bitstream. Both are barrel-shifter operations. The shift width and the bitstream reader's buffer depth are not published. Standard construction for the shifter; the renormalisation rule is a spec fact.
- **Adder tree + multiplier array (inverse-transform butterflies)** — Reconstruction inverts the encoder's transform: AV1's 16 separable 2-D kernels (DCT, ADST, flipped ADST, identity) at 19 scales from 64x64 to 4x4 (verified — libaom AV1 Encoder Guide; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3), applied as two one-dimensional passes — the spec's inverse transform process is a 1-D row pass followed by a 1-D column pass with butterfly functions (verified — AV1 spec, §7.13 Inverse transform process: "1D transforms", "Butterfly functions", "2D inverse transform process"; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). A butterfly stage is an adder tree with coefficient multipliers. Spec facts about the transform set; the butterfly depth and multiplier count are not published.
- **Multiplier array (motion-compensation 8-tap interpolation)** — Inter prediction on decode interpolates reference samples with the same 8-tap filters as the encoder: EIGHTTAP, EIGHTTAP_SMOOTH and EIGHTTAP_SHARP, eight taps summed per sample (verified — AV1 Bitstream & Decoding Process Specification v1.0.0 with Errata 1, §7.11.3 inter prediction; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). Each tap is a multiply, so the interpolator is a multiplier array feeding an adder tree. Spec fact about the algorithm; the array's width and tap parallelism are not published.
- **Comparator (CDEF direction detection and deblocking edge decisions)** — The in-loop filters decide where and how strongly to filter. CDEF is the "Constrained Directional Enhancement Filter designed to adaptively filter blocks based on identifying the direction" (verified — AV1 spec, §3; already recorded at Level 2), so it must first detect the dominant direction by comparing directional gradients; the deblocking loop filter is "A filtering process applied to the reconstruction intended to reduce the visibility of block edges" (verified — AV1 spec, §3; already recorded at Level 2), so it compares samples across each block edge to set its strength. Both decisions are comparator operations. The direction-detection and edge-strength circuits are not published. Spec facts about what the filters do; the comparators are standard construction.
- **Adder tree + multiplier array (CDEF and loop-restoration filter taps)** — After deblocking, AV1 applies CDEF and then loop restoration: "AV1 supports three types of post encode in loop filtering to improve the quality of the reconstructed video" — deblocking, CDEF, and loop restoration (verified — libaom AV1 Encoder Guide; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3), and the loop restoration filter "acts on units of either 64 x 64, 128 x 128, or 256 x 256 pixel blocks, refered to as loop restoration units. Each unit can independently select either to bypass filtering, use a Wiener filter, or use a self-guided filter." (verified — libaom AV1 Encoder Guide; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3). CDEF applies a primary filter along the detected direction and a secondary filter at 45 degrees to it (verified — libaom AV1 Encoder Guide: "A primary filter is applied along the selected direction, whilst a secondary filter is applied at 45 degrees to the primary direction."; new fact record this run). Every filter tap is a multiply-accumulate, so the filter stages are multiplier arrays feeding adder trees. Spec facts about the filter structure; tap counts, coefficient widths and the filter datapath are not published.
- **Mux / demux (decode session steering to a VCN instance)** — Decode sessions are steered to a VCN instance — on Navi 31- and Navi 32-class parts there are two, on Navi 33-class parts one (verified — already recorded at Level 2) — and the decoded frame is steered onward to the display engine or to a consumer (verified — already recorded at Level 2: the Level-2 trace). Both are mux/demux operations: sessions to instance 0 or 1, frames to display or memory. The steering fabric's radix, widths and arbitration are not published.
- **Counter (tile and frame sequencing)** — Frames are decoded tile by tile — the spec caps a tile grid at 64 rows by 64 columns (verified — AV1 spec, §3 constants: MAX_TILE_ROWS 64, "Maximum number of tile rows"; MAX_TILE_COLS 64, "Maximum number of tile columns"; already recorded for NVENC at Level 3) — so the decoder sequences tiles and blocks with row/column counters, and counts decoded frames for reference-frame management. The 64×64 cap is a spec fact; the sequencer's counter widths and the tile-scheduling policy are not published.
- **Pipeline register (inter-stage latches)** — Work is latched between entropy decode, reconstruction, inverse transform, in-loop filtering and the reference store so the pipeline sustains the published decode rates — AV1 to 8192x4352, HEVC and VP9 to 7680x4320 (verified — already recorded at Level 2). The stage count, latch widths and stage latencies are not published.

**Parameter honesty.** Parameter honesty: the published decode facts are the AMD contract (VCN 4.0 decode maxima AV1 8192x4352, HEVC and VP9 7680x4320, H.264 4096x2176 8-bit only; 2 VCN instances on gfx1100/gfx1102, 1 on gfx1101; simultaneous encode/decode streams up to 8K60 for HEVC; JPEG decode; decoded frames feeding the display engine directly) and the codec-spec facts (AV1 CDF probability times 32768, top entry 1 << 15, update count capped at 32; symbol decoding as a range/value state machine with renormalisation bits = 15 − FloorLog2(SymbolRange); 16 2-D inverse-transform kernels at 19 scales; 8-tap interpolation filters; CDEF as a direction-adaptive filter with a primary filter along the detected direction and a secondary filter at 45 degrees, and the loop filter as a block-edge filter; three in-loop filters with loop-restoration units of 64x64, 128x128 or 256x256, each bypass, Wiener or self-guided; tile grid capped at 64 rows by 64 columns). Below that level — reference-store capacity and banking, FIFO depths, table counts and per-session storage, decoder FSM state count and symbol rate, bitstream-reader buffer depth, butterfly depth and multiplier count, interpolator width, direction-detection and edge-strength circuits, filter tap counts and coefficient widths, steering mux radix, sequencer counter widths, stage count and latch widths — AMD publishes nothing, and this decomposition invents nothing.

#### Down to the gates: The dual media engines and the AV1 encode path — two whole encoders, one new codec

AMD publishes no gate-level structure for VCN 4.0 — no netlist, no standard-cell description, no transistor count for the RDNA 3 media engine. The deepest published description is the AMD RDNA 3 press release, the ROCm rocDecode capability table and the AMD GPUOpen AMF pre-analysis guide, which describe the pipeline stages, the API contract and the codec features at block level, and the codec specifications (AV1, HEVC, H.264), which define the algorithms the silicon must implement. What follows takes each Level-3 primitive down to gates and transistors: published spec geometry stays published, arithmetic from that geometry is labelled as arithmetic, and every gate form is the textbook-standard construction of that primitive, labelled as such — never a claim about AMD's circuits.

- **SRAM bank (reference frame store)** — The reference store is an SRAM bank in the primer's form: rows of 6T SRAM cells — two cross-coupled inverters (4 transistors) plus two access transistors — behind a row decoder (a NAND-gate tree selecting one wordline), transmission-gate column muxes (2 transistors per leg) and latch-type differential sense amplifiers. The published contract is the frame count: up to seven AV1 reference frames must be held while the motion estimator searches them, so the store is seven frames deep at minimum — but a frame's bit count depends on the session's resolution and format, which are runtime parameters, not published silicon geometry, so no cell total is claimed. Whether the store is one bank or one bank per reference, and its port count, are not published. Standard construction.
- **FIFO / queue (frame ingest and dual-engine handoff)** — A FIFO at gate level is a storage array plus two pointer counters plus full/empty comparators: the write pointer and read pointer are counters of N flip-flops plus N full adders each (a D flip-flop is about 20–28 transistors, a full adder about 28), incrementing on push and pop, and the full and empty flags are comparators over the pointer values — one XOR per compared bit feeding an AND tree. The ingest queue and the dual-engine handoff are FIFOs of this form, but their depths and widths are not published, so the pointer widths — and therefore the counter and comparator totals — are not claimed. The handoff itself is a demux steering one session to each of the two engines, counted in the mux primitive below. Standard construction.
- **Adder tree + comparator (motion-estimation SAD and best-match selection)** — A sum of absolute differences is subtractors, absolute-value logic and an adder tree: each per-pixel difference is a subtractor (one full adder per bit, about 28 transistors each, with the sign bit selecting the two's-complement negation through a mux), the absolute value is a conditional invert-and-increment, and the adder tree collapses the per-pixel differences pairwise — a tree of adders whose depth is log2 of the block size. The best-match selection is a comparator (one XOR per compared bit feeding an AND tree) holding the lowest cost so far, with a register holding the winning displacement. The candidate set, the search range, the block sizes searched and the SAD datapath width are not published, so no adder-tree or comparator total is claimed — only the form. Standard construction.
- **Multiplier array (motion-compensation 8-tap interpolation)** — Each interpolation tap is a multiply, and AV1's filters are 8-tap, so the interpolator is eight multipliers per sample lane feeding an adder tree: a multiplier is a partial-product AND array (one AND2 gate per partial product, 6 transistors each) plus an adder tree of full adders (about 28 transistors each) summing the partial products. The coefficient width is not published, so the multiplier bit width is not claimed, and the array's width and tap parallelism are not published, so no multiplier total is claimed — only the eight-taps-per-sample shape the spec fixes. Standard construction.
- **Adder tree + multiplier array (transform butterflies and quantisation)** — A butterfly stage is an adder tree of full adders (about 28 transistors each) with coefficient multipliers (a partial-product AND array plus an adder tree per multiplier), and quantisation is a further multiply by the reciprocal step — one multiplier per coefficient lane. The transform set is a spec fact: four separable 1-D transforms combinable into 16 2-D kernels at 19 scales from 64x64 down to 4x4, so a 64x64 butterfly is six stages deep by arithmetic (log2 of 64) and a 4x4 butterfly two stages deep. The butterfly depth as built, the multiplier count and the quantiser datapath are not published, so no gate total is claimed beyond the per-stage form. Standard construction.
- **Register file (CDF probability tables and CABAC context models)** — A register file at gate level is an array of D flip-flops — about 20–28 transistors per stored bit — behind a decoder (a NAND-gate tree selecting one entry) and read muxes (transmission gates, 2 transistors per leg). The table geometry is a spec fact: an AV1 CDF entry is a 15-bit value (probability times 32768, top entry 1 << 15), so 15 flip-flops per CDF entry, 300–420 transistors in the storage alone by arithmetic; a CABAC context model is one of 127 states, so 7 bits of state per model; the CDF update count is capped at 32, so a 5-bit counter (5 flip-flops plus 5 full adders, 240–280 transistors by arithmetic) tracks it. The table count, entry count and banking are not published, so no register-file total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **FSM / controller (the arithmetic coder state machine)** — An FSM at gate level is a state register of D flip-flops (about 20–28 transistors each, one per state bit) plus next-state logic (a NAND/NOR network) plus output logic. The coder's alphabet is a spec fact: AV1's M-ary symbol arithmetic coder takes integer M in [2, 14], so at least 4 state bits carry the symbol alphabet by arithmetic, and the range/value state machine renormalises after every symbol. The FSM's state count and the coder's symbol-per-clock rate are not published, so no flip-flop or gate total is claimed — only the state-register-plus-next-state-logic form. Standard construction.
- **Barrel shifter (range renormalisation and bitstream packing)** — A barrel shifter is log2(width) stages of 2:1 muxes — transmission-gate form (2 transistors per leg) or NAND/NOR-tree form (about 16 transistors per 2:1 mux) — each stage shifting by a power of two selected by one control bit. The renormalisation shift is a spec fact: bits = 15 − FloorLog2(SymbolRange), so the shift runs up to 15 positions on a 15-bit range, which is four mux stages by arithmetic (log2 of 16). The shift width and the bitstream packer's buffer depth are not published, so no mux total is claimed beyond the four-stage form. Standard construction.
- **Comparator (mode decision — best prediction mode)** — Mode decision compares rate-distortion costs pairwise through a comparator tree: each comparison is one XOR per compared bit feeding an AND tree, and the tree keeps the cheapest candidate. The mode space is a spec fact: 71 basic intra prediction modes and 56 single-frame inter prediction modes, plus compound modes, over block partitions from 128x128 down to 4x4 — so the tree must select among at least 127 single-frame candidates by arithmetic, though the encoder prunes that space before comparing. The cost metric, the candidate pruning and the comparator width are not published, so no comparator total is claimed — only the tree form. Standard construction.
- **Priority encoder (transform-coefficient scan and end-of-block)** — A priority encoder is log2(N) levels of AND/OR gates over a valid vector, reporting the index of the highest-priority set bit: here the coefficient-valid vector, whose last set bit is the end of block (eob = scan index of the last non-zero coefficient plus one, a spec fact). The scan tables are spec facts; the encoder's coefficient datapath width and the priority encoder's size are not published, so no gate total is claimed — only the log2-level AND/OR form. Standard construction.
- **Counter (rate-control budget and CDF update count)** — A counter at gate level is N D flip-flops (about 20–28 transistors each) plus an incrementer of N full adders (about 28 transistors each). The CDF update count is capped at 32 by the spec, so it is a 5-bit counter: 5 flip-flops plus 5 full adders, 240–280 transistors by arithmetic. The rate-control budget counter tracks bits spent against the frame budget, but its width and the budget arithmetic are not published, so no total is claimed for it — only the counter form and the 5-bit CDF counter arithmetic. Standard construction.
- **Mux / demux (session steering across the two VCN instances)** — A mux at gate level is transmission gates (2 transistors per input leg) or a NAND/NOR tree (about 16 transistors per 2:1 mux); a demux is the same gates run in reverse. Steering a session to instance 0 or 1 is a 2:1 mux per bit of the session path, and steering the two bitstreams back to their callers is the matching demux — 2 transistors per bit per path in transmission-gate form by arithmetic. The steering fabric's radix, widths and arbitration are not published, so no mux total is claimed beyond the per-bit form. Standard construction.
- **Accumulator array (pre-analysis content-activity metrics)** — An accumulator at gate level is a register of D flip-flops (about 20–28 transistors per bit) plus an adder of full adders (about 28 transistors per bit) summing the per-pixel activity into the per-block score, with one accumulator per block of the frame. The lookahead buffer holds 0 to 41 frames of those scores, so it is 42 frames deep at most by arithmetic (0 through 41), but the scores' bit width is not published. The accumulator widths, the block grid the metric is computed over and the lookahead buffer's storage form are not published, so no accumulator or buffer total is claimed — only the register-plus-adder form. Standard construction.

Honesty: AMD publishes the VCN 4.0 pipeline at stage level only — two media engines on Navi 31- and Navi 32-class parts, AV1 hardware encode, Xilinx content-adaptive machine learning, AMF pre-analysis with a 0–41 frame lookahead, encode rates 4K 180/240 fps and 8K 48/60 fps, no driver lock on encode sessions (Level-2 and Level-3 fact records) — and no gate-level structure for any part of the block appears in any AMD source. Everything below is the standard textbook construction of the named primitive, pointing at the primer's bottom layer; none of it is a claim about AMD's actual netlist (new Level-4 fact record: unverifiable).

#### Down to the gates: The decode pipeline — one unified core, bounded by the codec table

Decode is the inverse of the encode loop, carried out entirely in the fixed-function block — entropy decode, reconstruction against reference frames, in-loop filtering, and the frame's handoff to display or memory. AMD publishes no gate-level structure for the decode path either, so the decompositions below are the same textbook-standard forms as the encode block, applied to the decode primitives: published spec geometry stays published, arithmetic from that geometry is labelled as arithmetic, and every gate form is labelled standard construction — never a claim about AMD's circuits.

- **SRAM bank (reference frame store and decoded-frame buffer)** — The reference store is an SRAM bank in the primer's form: rows of 6T SRAM cells — two cross-coupled inverters (4 transistors) plus two access transistors — behind a row decoder (a NAND-gate tree selecting one wordline), transmission-gate column muxes (2 transistors per leg) and latch-type differential sense amplifiers. The published contract is the frame count: AV1 can reference up to seven frames (REFS_PER_FRAME 7, a spec fact), so the store is seven frames deep at minimum — but a frame's bit count depends on the session's resolution and format, which are runtime parameters, not published silicon geometry, so no cell total is claimed. Its capacity, banking and port count are not published. Standard construction.
- **FIFO / queue (bitstream ingest and session queueing)** — A FIFO at gate level is a storage array plus two pointer counters plus full/empty comparators: the write pointer and read pointer are counters of N flip-flops plus N full adders each (a D flip-flop is about 20–28 transistors, a full adder about 28), incrementing on push and pop, and the full and empty flags are comparators over the pointer values — one XOR per compared bit feeding an AND tree. The bitstream ingest path and the per-session state are FIFOs of this form, but queue depths, session-store size and the queueing mechanism are not published, so the pointer widths — and therefore the counter and comparator totals — are not claimed. Standard construction.
- **Register file (CDF tables and CABAC context state, per session)** — A register file at gate level is an array of D flip-flops — about 20–28 transistors per stored bit — behind a decoder (a NAND-gate tree selecting one entry) and read muxes (transmission gates, 2 transistors per leg). The table geometry is a spec fact: an AV1 CDF entry is a 15-bit value (probability times 32768, top entry 1 << 15), so 15 flip-flops per CDF entry, 300–420 transistors in the storage alone by arithmetic; a CABAC context model is one of 127 states, so 7 bits of state per model; the CDF update count is capped at 32, so a 5-bit counter (5 flip-flops plus 5 full adders, 240–280 transistors by arithmetic) tracks it — and each decode session carries its own copy of the tables. The table count and the per-session storage size are not published, so no register-file total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **FSM / controller (the symbol decoder state machine)** — An FSM at gate level is a state register of D flip-flops (about 20–28 transistors each, one per state bit) plus next-state logic (a NAND/NOR network) plus output logic. The decoder's control steps through range subdivision, renormalisation and CDF update for every symbol — the spec's symbol decoding process is a state machine over a CDF array of length N + 1, and CABAC's binary decoding loop is the same shape one bin at a time. The FSM's state count and symbols-per-clock rate are not published, so no flip-flop or gate total is claimed — only the state-register-plus-next-state-logic form. Standard construction.
- **Barrel shifter (renormalisation and literal bit reads)** — A barrel shifter is log2(width) stages of 2:1 muxes — transmission-gate form (2 transistors per leg) or NAND/NOR-tree form (about 16 transistors per 2:1 mux) — each stage shifting by a power of two selected by one control bit. The renormalisation shift is a spec fact: bits = 15 − FloorLog2(SymbolRange), so the shift runs up to 15 positions on a 15-bit range, which is four mux stages by arithmetic (log2 of 16); literal and uncompressed header values are read straight from the bitstream through the same shifter form. The shift width and the bitstream reader's buffer depth are not published, so no mux total is claimed beyond the four-stage form. Standard construction.
- **Adder tree + multiplier array (inverse-transform butterflies)** — A butterfly stage is an adder tree of full adders (about 28 transistors each) with coefficient multipliers (a partial-product AND array plus an adder tree per multiplier), applied as two one-dimensional passes — the spec's inverse transform process is a 1-D row pass followed by a 1-D column pass with butterfly functions. The transform set is a spec fact: 16 separable 2-D kernels at 19 scales from 64x64 to 4x4, so a 64x64 inverse butterfly is six stages deep by arithmetic (log2 of 64) and a 4x4 butterfly two stages deep. The butterfly depth as built and the multiplier count are not published, so no gate total is claimed beyond the per-stage form. Standard construction.
- **Multiplier array (motion-compensation 8-tap interpolation)** — Each interpolation tap is a multiply, and AV1's filters are 8-tap, so the interpolator is eight multipliers per sample lane feeding an adder tree: a multiplier is a partial-product AND array (one AND2 gate per partial product, 6 transistors each) plus an adder tree of full adders (about 28 transistors each) summing the partial products. The coefficient width is not published, so the multiplier bit width is not claimed, and the array's width and tap parallelism are not published, so no multiplier total is claimed — only the eight-taps-per-sample shape the spec fixes. Standard construction.
- **Comparator (CDEF direction detection and deblocking edge decisions)** — A comparator at gate level is one XOR per compared bit feeding an AND tree. CDEF detects the dominant direction by comparing directional gradients — one comparator per gradient pair — and the deblocking loop filter compares samples across each block edge to set its strength — one comparator per edge sample pair. The direction-detection and edge-strength circuits are not published, so no comparator count is claimed — only the XOR-plus-AND-tree form per comparison. Standard construction.
- **Adder tree + multiplier array (CDEF and loop-restoration filter taps)** — Every filter tap is a multiply-accumulate: a multiplier (a partial-product AND array plus an adder tree of full adders, about 28 transistors each) feeding an accumulation adder (one full adder per bit). The filter structure is a spec fact: CDEF applies a primary filter along the detected direction and a secondary filter at 45 degrees to it, and loop restoration acts on units of 64x64, 128x128 or 256x256 pixels, each unit independently selecting bypass, a Wiener filter or a self-guided filter — so a 64x64 loop-restoration unit holds 4,096 pixels by arithmetic, each filtered by its taps. Tap counts, coefficient widths and the filter datapath are not published, so no gate total is claimed beyond the per-tap multiply-accumulate form. Standard construction.
- **Mux / demux (decode session steering to a VCN instance)** — A mux at gate level is transmission gates (2 transistors per input leg) or a NAND/NOR tree (about 16 transistors per 2:1 mux); a demux is the same gates run in reverse. Steering a decode session to instance 0 or 1 is a 2:1 mux per bit of the session path, and steering the decoded frame onward to the display engine or to a consumer is the matching demux — 2 transistors per bit per path in transmission-gate form by arithmetic. The steering fabric's radix, widths and arbitration are not published, so no mux total is claimed beyond the per-bit form. Standard construction.
- **Counter (tile and frame sequencing)** — A counter at gate level is N D flip-flops (about 20–28 transistors each) plus an incrementer of N full adders (about 28 transistors each). The tile grid is capped by the spec at 64 rows by 64 columns (MAX_TILE_ROWS 64, MAX_TILE_COLS 64), so the row counter and the column counter are each 6 bits: 6 flip-flops plus 6 full adders, 288–336 transistors per counter by arithmetic. The sequencer's counter widths beyond the cap and the tile-scheduling policy are not published, so no further total is claimed — only the two 6-bit counter arithmetic. Standard construction.
- **Pipeline register (inter-stage latches)** — A pipeline register at gate level is one D flip-flop per latched bit — about 20–28 transistors each — latching work between entropy decode, reconstruction, inverse transform, in-loop filtering and the reference store so the pipeline sustains the published decode rates (AV1 to 8192x4352, HEVC and VP9 to 7680x4320). The stage count, latch widths and stage latencies are not published, so no flip-flop total is claimed — only the one-D-flip-flop-per-bit form. Standard construction.

Honesty: AMD publishes the VCN 4.0 decode path at contract level only — decode maxima AV1 8192x4352, HEVC and VP9 7680x4320, H.264 capped 4096x2176 (Level-2 fact records) — and no gate-level structure for any part of the block appears in any AMD source. Everything below is the standard textbook construction of the named primitive, pointing at the primer's bottom layer; none of it is a claim about AMD's actual netlist (new Level-4 fact record: unverifiable).
**How work flows.** Frames arrive from GPU memory: The AMF runtime queues an encode/decode job; the block DMAs frames from VRAM. Codec core processes macroblocks: Motion search, transform and entropy stages run in fixed function at the codec's native rates (AV1 to 8K60 on Navi 3x-class parts). Bitstream exits: Encoded streams return to memory for the application; decode feeds the display engine directly. Second engine takes the next session: On dual-VCN parts, a parallel transcode starts without disturbing the first.

**Trade-off accepted.** Quality-per-bit at launch. VCN 4.0's AV1 encode checked the box, but early H.264 quality still trailed NVENC/Quick Sync in reviewers' tests, and a documented AV1 encode quirk at exact 1080p required padded internal resolutions. Fixed-function media ages by standard, not by benchmark: VCN 4.0 has no VVC path.
