One APU serves three precisions and three coprocessor roles, so a mux selects the INT8, INT16 or FP16 datapath for the inference at hand — a 3:1 select, 2 2:1 muxes in 2 stages by arithmetic — a second steers the frame to the photo AI-NR path or the 4K HDR video AI-NR path, a 2:1 select, and a third routes the APU's work between its AI-ISP, AI-GPU and AI-Video roles, a 3:1 select — five 2:1 muxes in total by arithmetic. The mux widths and select encoding are not published, so no further mux total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Priority encoder / arbiter (APU workload arbitration among AI-ISP, AI-GPU and AI-Video)** — A priority encoder is a tree of OR gates with a priority chain: N request lines reduce to a grant index naming the highest-priority active request, with a round-robin variant adding a rotating priority register of D flip-flops. The APU 590 is shared with gaming, social video and every other AI workload, so an arbiter decides which workload's inference runs next when several are ready — the APU-dependency cost the Level-2 bottleneck section names — and a priority encoder turns the winning request into the task index the APU's scheduler sees — a 3-way select among AI-ISP, AI-GPU and AI-Video needs a 2-bit index (arithmetic — 2 to the 1st is 2, below 3, and 2 to the 2nd is 4, the smallest power of two above it). The arbitration policy is not published, so no further encoder total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **FSM / controller (APU-ISP fusion sequencer; AI-NR inference state machine; power-state controller)** — A finite-state machine is state bits plus next-state logic plus output logic: the state bits are master-slave D flip-flops (about 20–28 transistors each) and the next-state and output logic is a NAND/NOR network driven by the current state and the inputs. The five documented functions run in order, so a controller sequences the fusion — frame out of the ISP, inference on the APU, denoised frame back, HDR shaping, output — an inference state machine walks the AI-NR model layer by layer, and a power-state controller holds the APU inside the efficiency envelope that makes per-frame denoise affordable on a phone. Each is a state machine of this form. The state counts and sequencing are not published, so no state-bit total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Pipeline registers (between ISP output, APU inference and return stages)** — A pipeline register is one D flip-flop per bit — about 20–28 transistors each, two cross-coupled latch stages — latched between stages so the next stage can start while the current stage's result is held. Each fusion stage hands its result to the next through pipeline registers, so the ISP can expose the next frame while the APU denoises the current one and the encoder takes the previous one — the overlap that keeps the 4K HDR video path running instead of stopping for each inference. The register widths and stage count are not published, so no register total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Counter (tile index counter across the 4K frame; inference-frame counter)** — A counter is N D flip-flops plus N full adders in a ripple or look-ahead chain, incrementing on each clock, with a comparator resetting it at the terminal count. The denoise counts what it processes: a tile index counter steps across the frame's tiles — one 4K frame is 8,294,400 pixels (arithmetic), so the tile count follows the tiling the model uses, which MediaTek does not publish — and an inference-frame counter tracks the sequence of frames handed to the APU. No counter width is claimed, because the tile size is not published. Standard construction.
- **Synchronizer (ISP clock domain vs APU 590 domain crossing)** — A synchronizer is two D flip-flops in series — about 20–28 transistors each — the first sampling the incoming signal in the new clock domain and the second re-sampling it a cycle later so metastability resolves before the value is used; a multi-bit crossing is an asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers, the pointers changing one bit at a time so a sampled pointer is never more than one count stale. The ISP and the APU 590 do not share one clock, so synchronizers carry the frame into the APU's domain and the denoised frame back again, in the standard two-flop construction. The domain frequencies and synchronizer depths are not published, so no synchronizer total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Credit counter (APU compute-budget allocation shared with gaming and social video; per-frame inference budget)** — A credit counter is a down-counter of D flip-flops and full adders with a comparator: it starts at the budget, decrements on each issued request and increments on each returned credit, and a comparator blocks new requests when the count reaches zero. Every frame's denoise is an inference that must fit the phone's power budget, and the APU is shared, so a credit counter budgets APU compute between AI-ISP, AI-GPU and AI-Video work — holding back the denoise when the frame's inference budget is spent so gaming and social video keep their share. The credit limits and the counter widths are not published, so no counter total is claimed. Standard construction.

Honesty: MediaTek publishes the AI-NR + APU 590 fusion at function level only — the AI-NR photo stage, 4K HDR video with AI-NR, the APU 590 as the compute partner, the AI 3A and AI-HDR and AI-FD statistics, and the power-efficiency envelope (Level-2 and Level-3 fact records) — and no gate-level structure for any part of the fusion appears in any MediaTek source. Everything below is the standard textbook construction of the named primitive, pointing at the primer's bottom layer; none of it is a claim about MediaTek's actual netlist (new Level-4 fact record: unverifiable).

### Samsung Exynos 2400 ISP

**Specs (wiki card).** Deca-core SoC ISP · 320 MP · AI zoom

**Building blocks.**
- **ISP front-end — 320 MP class** — Samsung publishes no name or block diagram for the Exynos 2400's ISP; what it documents is capability: single-camera support to 320 MP, dual-camera 64+32 MP, and 8K video (8K30 encode, 8K60 decode; Galaxy S24 phones record 8K at 30 fps)
- **Quad Bayer remosaic path** — The pipeline stage Galaxy photography actually runs on: 200 MP ISOCELL sensors bin and remosaic — reconstructing full-resolution colour from Quad/Tetra Bayer layouts in hardware, the default stills path on the S24 line
- **Zoom Anyplace engine ★** — Samsung's AI zoom stage, built around the 200 MP sensor: it tracks a moving subject and crops a 4× close-up from the full-resolution stream without the quality collapse of digital zoom — remosaic plus AI tracking sold as one feature
- **NPU complex (2× GNPU + 2× SNPU) as ISP partner** — The Exynos 2400's AI engine — two general NPUs and two shallow NPUs, 17K MAC class per secondary reporting — runs the learned stages (scene optimisation, AI zoom assistance) beside the ISP; Samsung quotes 14.7× the AI performance of Exynos 2200 without publishing a TOPS figure
- **Multi-frame HDR + video path** — Staggered HDR fusion and the 8K encode feed (AV1 decode supported; encode to 8K class) shared with the SoC's media block

**The piece that makes it special.** The remosaic is the product. With 200 MP Quad-Bayer sensors, 'the ISP' mostly means one stage — reconstructing believable full-colour detail from a sensor that never sees a full-colour pixel — plus the AI tracking that makes a 4× crop follow a moving subject. Samsung's disclosure posture is the other lesson: it markets outcomes (Zoom Anyplace, 14.7× AI) and withholds the ISP's name, blocks and the NPU's TOPS, so an honest breakdown is short where rivals' are long.

**How work flows.** 200 MP stream enters: The ISOCELL sensor delivers Quad-Bayer RAW at full or binned resolution. Remosaic reconstructs: The ISP rebuilds full-colour pixels; binning modes trade resolution for light. AI stages assist: NPU stages run scene optimisation and subject tracking for Zoom Anyplace crops. HDR fuses, video encodes: Multi-frame HDR merges for stills; video exits to the 8K-class encoder.

**Trade-off accepted.** Disclosure. Almost everything quantitative about this ISP beyond sensor ceilings comes from launch-event reporting and teardowns, not a Samsung datasheet — including the NPU's structure. Where Samsung publishes no number (NPU TOPS, ISP throughput), this entry says so instead of repeating the rumoured figures as fact.

**Fact check.**
- [corrected] The entry previously said the ISP supports "8K60-class recording" — Source: FoneArena Exynos 2400 spec list + SamMobile spec table + Android Authority launch coverage. Was: 8K60-class recording; now: 8K30 encode, 8K60 decode. Quote: "Up to 8K decoding: 60fps with 10-bit HEVC(H.265), VP9, AV1, Up to 8K encoding: 30fps with 10-bit HEVC(H.265), VP9" Note: 8K60 is decode/playback, not encode; Galaxy S24 phones record 8K at 30 fps.
- [verified] ISP supports up to 320 MP sensors; Zoom Anyplace gives 4× close-ups of moving objects from a 200 MP sensor — Source: Samsung System LSI Tech Day 2023 — Exynos 2400 showcase (Samsung). Quote: "Samsung introduced the Zoom Anyplace technology, powered by a 200-million-pixel image sensor, enabling users to capture 4x close-ups of moving objects without image degradation."
- [unverifiable] NPU structure (2 GNPU + 2 SNPU, ~17K MAC) and any TOPS figure — Source: Secondary reporting (Notebookcheck / launch coverage). Note: Samsung quotes only a 14.7× AI uplift vs Exynos 2200; it publishes no NPU TOPS or ISP block diagram for Exynos 2400.
- [unverifiable] **Samsung Exynos 2400 ISP** — No gate-level structure for the Exynos 2400 ISP is published by Samsung — no netlist, standard-cell description or transistor count for the Tetra2pixel binning, the remosaic, the E2E AI Remosaic parallelism, the Smart-ISO Pro plus DSG HDR merge, the Super QPD autofocus, the deep-learning fusion engine or the Zoom Anyplace tracking; the Level-4 decomposition is the textbook-standard construction of each Level-3 primitive, not a claim about Samsung's circuits. Source: Samsung Introduces the 200-Megapixel Image Sensor for the Ultimate High Resolution Experience in Flagship Smartphones (Samsung Newsroom, Jan 17, 2023); Samsung Electronics Introduces ISOCELL Zoom Anyplace & E2E AI Remosaic Solutions for the 200-Megapixel Image Sensor (Samsung Newsroom, Oct 31, 2023).

#### Inside the signature block: Tetra2pixel remosaic and E2E AI Remosaic — the 200 MP stills path

**Inside it.** Samsung publishes no ISP block diagram, no per-stage latency, no queue depths and no ISP throughput figure for the Exynos 2400, so these are Samsung's documented functions in pipeline order, not die sub-blocks. (1) Tetra2pixel binning modes, on the ISOCELL HP2 sensor: full 200 MP in bright light, 4-in-1 binning to 50 MP at 1.2 μm, or 16-in-1 binning to 12.5 MP at 2.4 μm in low light. (2) Remosaic: the array-conversion stage that rebuilds full-colour pixels from the Quad Bayer layout of same-colour pixel groups. (3) E2E AI Remosaic: remosaic and ISP run simultaneously instead of in sequence, cutting remosaic latency by up to half. (4) Smart-ISO Pro plus DSG HDR: DSG applies two separate conversion values to the analog signal in 50 MP mode, and Smart-ISO Pro merges different ISO readouts from a single exposure for 12.5 MP stills and 4K60 HDR video. (5) Super QPD autofocus: all 200 million pixels act as focusing agents, grouped by four adjacent pixels to read horizontal and vertical pattern changes. (6) Deep-learning fusion engine plus hardware noise reduction: named on Samsung's Exynos 2400 spec sheet as reported at launch, with no block diagram or throughput figure published.

**Trace — one unit of work: one 200 MP still — photon to JPEG.**
1. **Light lands on 200 million 0.6 μm pixels. **The ISOCELL HP2 holds 200 million 0.6 μm pixels in a 1/1.3-inch optical format, and Tetra2pixel picks the mode: full 200 MP in bright light, 50 MP at 1.2 μm or 12.5 MP at 2.4 μm binned in low light. D-VTG adds a second transfer gate in each pixel, lifting full-well capacity by more than 33 percent so highlights hold instead of washing out.
2. **The sensor bins, then outputs raw. **In 50 MP mode DSG applies two separate conversion values to the analog signal at the pixel level, and Super QPD has already used all 200 million pixels as focusing agents to lock focus before the shot. The raw frame leaves the sensor for the ISP.
3. **Remosaic rebuilds colour from the Quad Bayer array. **Array-conversion processing turns the groups of same-colour pixels into full-colour pixels. A 200 MP frame carries 16,384 by 12,288 samples to convert, which is why this stage, not the sensor, sets the pace of the stills path.
4. **Remosaic and ISP now run at the same time. **E2E AI Remosaic runs remosaic and ISP simultaneously instead of in sequence, reducing remosaic latency by up to half. The old pipeline was raw output, then remosaic, then ISP, then JPEG, all in sequence.
5. **HDR merges and the fusion engine finishes the frame. **Smart-ISO Pro merges different ISO readouts from a single exposure for HDR, the deep-learning fusion engine and hardware noise reduction clean the result, and the NPU beside the ISP runs scene optimisation on the finished frame.
6. **A JPEG exits and the shutter is ready sooner. **Faster overall processing means less data loss from latency and richer detail and colour, in Samsung's words, and the user-visible win is shorter shooting time on 200 MP images. The stills path's cost is now paid in parallel compute and memory bandwidth, not in serial waiting.

**Bottleneck in / out.** Relieves the sequential remosaic tax: at 200 MP the remosaic-then-ISP chain made every full-resolution still pay a long serial latency, the shutter lag users felt, and E2E parallelism cuts the remosaic latency by up to half. Creates two new bottlenecks instead: the parallel stages now demand bandwidth and compute at the same time, so the ISP and the remosaic engine contend for the same memory path while a 200 MP frame is in flight; and the sensor itself, since a 0.6 μm pixel gathers little light, so low-light quality still depends on binning resolution away to 50 MP or 12.5 MP rather than on any ISP stage.

**Governing numbers.** 200 MP sensor, 16,384 x 12,288, 0.6 μm pixels in a 1/1.3-inch optical format; Tetra2pixel: 4-in-1 gives 50 MP at 1.2 μm, 16-in-1 gives 12.5 MP at 2.4 μm; 8K video from the 50 MP mode at 30 fps, about 33 MP; D-VTG boosts full-well capacity by more than 33 percent; E2E AI Remosaic reduces remosaic latency by up to half; ISP ceilings: 320 MP single camera, 108 MP at 30 fps zero-shutter-lag, 64+32 MP dual camera at 30 fps; 8K30 encode, 8K60 decode.

**Primary source.** Samsung Newsroom, 'Samsung Introduces the 200-Megapixel Image Sensor for the Ultimate High Resolution Experience in Flagship Smartphones' (Jan 17, 2023) — 'The ISOCELL HP2 packs 200-million 0.6-micrometer (μm) pixels in a 1/1.3” optical format, a sensor size that is widely used in 108MP main smartphone cameras.'; 'When in low-lit environments, the sensor transforms either into a 1.2μm 50MP or 2.4μm 12.5MP image sensor by binding four to 16 neighboring pixels.'; 'For fuller 8K video, approximately at 33MP, the HP2 switches to 1.2μm 50MP mode to minimize cropping and capture more of the scene. Filming 8K at 30 frames-per-second (fps), a wide field of view along with bigger pixel size can produce sharp cinematic videos.'; 'With high precision, D-VTG adds a second transfer gate in the pixel, boosting the pixel’s full-well capacity by more than 33 percent.'; 'In low-lit settings, the HP2’s auto-focusing is taken to the next level with Super QPD, which allows the sensor to use all its 200-million pixels for focusing agents.'; 'Samsung is introducing the DSG feature for the first time in 50MP mode which applies two separate conversion values to the analog signal received at the pixel level.'; 'In addition, the Smart-ISO Pro, an HDR solution that merges different levels of ISO readouts from a single exposure, allows the camera to take 12.5MP images and 4K at 60fps video in HDR.' Samsung Newsroom, 'Samsung Electronics Introduces ISOCELL Zoom Anyplace & E2E AI Remosaic Solutions for the 200-Megapixel Image Sensor' (Oct 31, 2023) — 'Currently, the steps the 200MP image sensor follows for processing images after shooting are: raw data output occurs before a remosaic, which then leads to image signal processing (ISP) before finishing with JPEG image output. In this process, all of the steps occur in sequence.'; 'E2E AI Remosaic improves the process by enabling the remosaic and ISP to take place simultaneously. In other words, E2E AI Remosaic takes a process that occurs in sequence and makes it occur in parallel, thereby reducing remosaic latency by up to half.' ISP ceilings (320 MP, 108 MP at 30 fps, 64+32 MP dual, 8K30 encode, 8K60 decode) are secondary reporting only — SamMobile Exynos 2400 spec table and Android Authority launch coverage; Samsung publishes no public Exynos 2400 datasheet with these figures.

#### Inside the signature block: Zoom Anyplace — in-sensor zoom with AI subject tracking

**Inside it.** Samsung publishes no ISP block diagram and no per-stage latency for this feature either, so these are Samsung's documented functions in order, not die sub-blocks. (1) Subject selection plus AI tracking: the user selects a subject and the AI engine finds it, tracks it and follows it, so even fast-moving subjects stay in frame. Samsung's published account pairs the tracking with the Qualcomm AI engine; the Exynos 2400's own AI engine is the 2x GNPU plus 2x SNPU NPU, and Samsung has not published a separate Exynos-side account of the feature. (2) ROI selection from the full scope: the zoomed area is selected from the entire 200 MP scope, even at the edge of the frame, without changing the full-scope filming angle. (3) Real-time remosaic of the ROI: the selected area is remosaiced in real time so the zoomed view keeps the original 12.5 MP resolution. (4) Dual-stream capture: the full field of view and the zoomed-in view are filmed at the same time, both at high resolution — up to 4K per secondary reporting of Samsung's demo. (5) Stabilization: videos are shot with less screen shake while the tracking owns the subject. Status at announcement: Samsung's October 2023 article presents Zoom Anyplace as a solution for the 200 MP sensor and footnotes its images as illustrative of a technology still in development; no Galaxy model is named as shipping it in that article.

**Trace — one unit of work: one video frame — full view plus 4x close-up.**
1. **The user taps a subject on the 200 MP frame. **Selection is the only input: the user picks the desired subject and from here the camera owns it, tracking and filming it without the user having to follow it by hand.
2. **The AI engine finds the subject and locks on. **The tracking engine finds a moving subject and follows it, ensuring it is not missed during filming, and even fast-moving subjects are prevented from going off-screen. Samsung's published demo runs this tracking on the Qualcomm AI engine.
3. **The zoom window is cut from the full sensor scope. **The area to zoom in on is selected from the entire 200 MP scope, not from a binned frame, and even a subject on the edge of the screen can be zoomed in on without modifying the angle of the full-scope filming.
4. **Real-time remosaic rebuilds the zoomed window. **The selected area is remosaiced in real time, so the zoomed view maintains the original 12.5 MP resolution instead of collapsing to the 0.78 MP a 4x digital zoom would give from a 12.5 MP sum mode.
5. **Two streams record at once. **The full field of view and the zoomed-in view are filmed simultaneously at high resolution, both up to 4K per secondary reporting of Samsung's demo. The 200 MP wide camera zooms 2x or 4x with no drop-off in resolution and no wide-to-tele switch mid-recording.
6. **Stabilization steadies both views. **Videos are shot with less screen shake, the subject stays in frame while it moves, and the user can zoom in or out freely while recording, or start zoomed in and then zoom out, so one scene is recorded in two ways from one camera.

**Bottleneck in / out.** Relieves the digital-zoom collapse: cropping a 12.5 MP binned frame 4x leaves 0.78 MP, and switching from wide to tele at 3x changes angle and quality mid-shot, while in-sensor zoom keeps the original 12.5 MP and holds one angle through 2x and 4x. Creates three new bottlenecks instead: two simultaneous high-resolution streams plus real-time remosaic plus tracking inference all draw on the same AI engine and memory bandwidth at once; the feature only exists where the full 200 MP scope exists, so it is a main-camera trick, not a system-wide zoom; and the tracking is only as good as the AI engine's subject model — lose the subject and the zoomed stream has nothing to follow.

**Governing numbers.** 200 MP sensor scope; 2x and 4x in-sensor zoom with no drop-off in resolution; 4x close-ups of moving objects without image degradation; digital-zoom baseline: 4x on a 12.5 MP sum mode gives 0.78 MP (12.5/16); full and zoomed views filmed simultaneously at high resolution, both up to 4K per secondary reporting of Samsung's demo; tracking keeps even fast-moving subjects in frame.

**Primary source.** Samsung Newsroom, 'Samsung Electronics Introduces ISOCELL Zoom Anyplace & E2E AI Remosaic Solutions for the 200-Megapixel Image Sensor' (Oct 31, 2023) — 'With the new solution for 200MP image sensors, users can select the desired subject and the camera will automatically track and film it.'; 'But with ISOCELL Zoom Anyplace and Qualcomm AI engine, the camera quickly finds a moving subject and tracks and follows it, ensuring that it is not missed during filming.'; 'ISOCELL Zoom Anyplace allows users to simultaneously capture the full field of view and zoomed-in areas on video.'; 'Previously, with digital zoom, if the center region of interest (ROI) area was zoomed in 4x at a 12.5MP sum mode, it theoretically resulted in 0.78MP (12.5MP/16) image resolution. With in-sensor zoom, however, the selected area to be zoomed in on is selected from the entire scope and remosaiced, which allows the sensor to maintain the original 12.5MP resolution and enable video to be shot much more vividly.'; 'However, the 200MP wide camera can seamlessly zoom in at 2x or even 4x with no drop off in resolution.' Samsung Newsroom, System LSI Tech Day 2023 (Oct 5, 2023) — 'Samsung introduced the Zoom Anyplace technology, powered by a 200-million-pixel image sensor, enabling users to capture 4x close-ups of moving objects without image degradation.' Both views up to 4K is secondary reporting only: Android Authority, 'Samsung's new zoom trick does something a smartphone has never done' — 'both full-view and zoomed-in areas can be recorded in up to 4K.'


#### Down to the primitives: Tetra2pixel remosaic and E2E AI Remosaic — the 200 MP stills path

The stills-path block runs Samsung's six documented functions in pipeline order — Tetra2pixel binning, remosaic, E2E AI Remosaic parallelism, Smart-ISO Pro plus DSG HDR, Super QPD autofocus and the deep-learning fusion engine with hardware noise reduction — and each step is built from the primitives below. Where a primitive's geometry is not published, that is stated plainly.

- **FIFO / queue (sensor readout staging; remosaic-to-ISP handoff queue; JPEG output queue)** — The raw frame leaves the sensor for the ISP, so a readout FIFO stages the sensor stream while the remosaic works the previous frame, decoupling the sensor readout rate from the remosaic rate. E2E AI Remosaic runs remosaic and ISP simultaneously instead of in sequence, so a handoff queue sits between the two parallel stages, absorbing the rate mismatch while both run at once, and the finished frame waits in an output queue for the JPEG encoder. The queue depths and the readout width are not published.

- **SRAM bank / line buffers (Quad Bayer neighbourhood store for array conversion; 200 MP frame staging)** — Remosaic rebuilds full-colour pixels from groups of same-colour pixels in the Quad Bayer layout, so the conversion cannot work on one pixel alone — line buffers hold the neighbouring rows while the array conversion runs, and the frame itself is staged on chip while the parallel remosaic and ISP stages work it. A 200 MP frame carries 16,384 by 12,288 samples to convert, which is why this stage, not the sensor, sets the pace of the stills path. The line-buffer depth, banking, port counts and widths are not published.

- **Multiplier array (remosaic interpolation weights; Smart-ISO Pro merge weighting)** — Rebuilding a full-colour pixel from its same-colour neighbours is interpolation, and interpolation is multiply work: each neighbour is weighted before the sum, and Smart-ISO Pro merges different ISO readouts from a single exposure the same way, weighting each readout before the merge. The array dimensions, lane count and number format are not published.

- **Adder tree (Tetra2pixel binning sums, 4-in-1 and 16-in-1; remosaic interpolation sums; Smart-ISO Pro merge sums)** — Binning is addition: 4-in-1 binning sums four neighbouring pixels into one 50 MP pixel, 16-in-1 binning sums sixteen into one 12.5 MP pixel, and an adder tree collapses each group — the standard construction — while the remosaic interpolation and the Smart-ISO Pro merge sum their weighted values the same way. The tree depth and width are not published.

- **Comparator (binning-mode selection thresholds; highlight clip and D-VTG full-well thresholds; Smart-ISO Pro ISO merge thresholds)** — Choosing the binning mode is a comparison: bright light stays at full 200 MP, low light bins to 50 MP or 12.5 MP, and the light level is judged against thresholds. D-VTG adds a second transfer gate in each pixel, lifting full-well capacity by more than 33 percent, so highlights are judged against the raised full-well threshold before they wash out, and Smart-ISO Pro compares its ISO readouts to decide which contributes to each pixel. The comparator count, widths and threshold values are not published.

- **Priority encoder / arbiter (remosaic vs ISP memory-path arbitration — the E2E contention the Level-2 bottleneck names)** — E2E AI Remosaic runs the remosaic and the ISP at the same time, so the two stages contend for the same memory path while a 200 MP frame is in flight — the new bottleneck the Level-2 section names — and an arbiter decides which stage's access moves next when both are ready at once, with a priority encoder turning the winning request into the access index the memory controller sees. The arbitration policy is not published.

- **Mux / demux (binning-mode select full vs 4-in-1 vs 16-in-1; remosaic vs bypass; stills vs video path select)** — One pipeline serves three binning modes, so a mux selects full 200 MP, 4-in-1 50 MP or 16-in-1 12.5 MP output from the sensor, a second steers the frame through the remosaic or past it, and a third steers the finished frame to the stills JPEG path or the 4K60 HDR video path that Smart-ISO Pro also serves. The mux widths and select encoding are not published.

- **FSM / controller (stills-path sequencer; E2E parallel-stage synchronisation controller; binning-mode controller)** — The six documented functions run in order, so a controller sequences the stills path — binning, remosaic, ISP, HDR merge, fusion, JPEG — a second controller keeps the remosaic and the ISP running in parallel without one overtaking the other, and a binning-mode controller picks the Tetra2pixel mode from the light level. The state counts and sequencing are not published.

- **Pipeline registers (between binning, remosaic, ISP, fusion and JPEG stages; E2E overlap registers)** — Each stills stage hands its result to the next through pipeline registers, so binning, remosaic, ISP, fusion and JPEG can overlap on successive frames instead of running one frame end to end — and the E2E overlap registers are what let the remosaic and the ISP run simultaneously, the structure that cuts the remosaic latency by up to half. The register widths and stage count are not published.

- **Counter (pixel counter to the 200 MP frame; binning-mode index; row and column counters)** — The stills path counts what it processes: the pixel counter runs across the 200 MP frame — 16,384 by 12,288 samples is 201,326,592 pixels (arithmetic), so the counter is 28 bits wide (arithmetic — 2 to the 27th is 134,217,728, below 201,326,592, and 2 to the 28th is 268,435,456, the smallest power of two above it) — the binning-mode index steps across the three Tetra2pixel modes, 2 bits wide (arithmetic — 2 to the 1st is 2, below 3, and 2 to the 2nd is 4), and row and column counters track the frame position, 14 bits each (arithmetic — 2 to the 14th is 16,384, the column count, and 2 to the 13th is 8,192, below the 12,288 row count, so 14 bits covers both). No other counter width is claimed.

- **Barrel shifter (bit-depth scaling from remosaic output toward JPEG and ISP depth; DSG dual-conversion scaling)** — DSG applies two separate conversion values to the analog signal in 50 MP mode, and the remosaic output has to be scaled toward the depth the ISP and the JPEG encoder take, so a barrel shifter shifts each value by a variable amount in one step to scale the depth. The shifter width is not published.

- **Synchronizer (sensor clock domain vs ISP domain; NPU handoff for scene optimisation)** — The sensor, the ISP and the NPU beside the ISP do not share one clock, so synchronizers carry the raw frame into the ISP's domain and the finished frame out again to the NPU for scene optimisation, in the standard two-flop construction. The domain frequencies and synchronizer depths are not published.

- **Credit counter (memory-bandwidth budget shared by the parallel remosaic and ISP stages)** — The parallel stages now demand bandwidth at the same time, so a credit counter budgets the shared memory path between the remosaic and the ISP — holding back one stage when its credits are spent so the other keeps its share — the mechanism behind the contention the Level-2 bottleneck section names. The credit limits and the counter widths are not published, so no counter total is claimed. Standard construction.

**Parameter honesty.** Honesty: Samsung publishes no Exynos 2400 ISP block diagram, no per-stage latency, no queue depths and no ISP throughput figure, so the primitives below are mapped from the documented functions in pipeline order of the Samsung Newsroom ISOCELL HP2 and ISOCELL Zoom Anyplace and E2E AI Remosaic articles, not from a die diagram. Every published figure is already recorded at Level 2; no new chip-specific number is claimed here. The only new numbers are counter widths computed from published figures and labelled arithmetic. Generic constructions are labelled standard construction.

#### Down to the primitives: Zoom Anyplace — in-sensor zoom with AI subject tracking

The Zoom Anyplace block runs Samsung's five documented functions in order — subject selection plus AI tracking, ROI selection from the full scope, real-time remosaic of the ROI, dual-stream capture and stabilization — and each step is built from the primitives below. Where a primitive's geometry is not published, that is stated plainly.

- **FIFO / queue (full-stream and zoom-stream queues to the encoder; tracking-result queue from the AI engine to the ROI selector)** — Two streams record at once, so each stream waits in its own queue for the encoder, absorbing the rate mismatch between the sensor and the encoder, and the AI engine's tracking result — where the subject is in this frame — waits in a queue for the ROI selector that cuts the zoom window. The queue depths and widths are not published.

- **SRAM bank / register file (ROI window store; subject-model feature store; dual-stream frame store)** — The zoom window is cut from the entire 200 MP scope, so the selected area is held in a store while it is remosaiced in real time, the tracking model holds the subject's features in a store read out as each frame is searched, and the full and zoomed frames are staged side by side while both record. The store capacities, banking, port counts and widths are not published.

- **Multiplier array (tracking inference multiply-accumulates on the AI engine; ROI remosaic interpolation; stabilization scaling)** — Tracking is inference: the AI engine runs multiply-accumulate work over the subject model and the frame to find the subject and follow it, the ROI remosaic interpolates the selected area back to full colour with multiply work of its own, and stabilization scales its motion correction the same way. The array dimensions, lane count and number format are not published, and Samsung has not published a separate Exynos-side account of the tracking compute.

The tree depth and width are not published.

- **Comparator (subject-match thresholds; ROI edge thresholds; stabilization motion thresholds)** — Tracking is a judgement call made by comparison: the AI engine compares each candidate region against the subject model and keeps the one that matches, the ROI selector compares the subject position against the frame edge — even a subject on the edge of the screen can be zoomed in on — and stabilization compares frame-to-frame motion against the shake threshold before it corrects. The comparator count, widths and threshold values are not published.

- **Mux / demux (full-view vs zoomed-view stream select; 2x vs 4x zoom select; ROI crop select)** — One camera records one scene two ways, so a mux steers the full field of view to one encoder path and the zoomed-in view to another, a second selects the 2x or 4x in-sensor zoom, and a third selects the ROI crop out of the full 200 MP scope. The mux widths and select encoding are not published.

The arbitration policy is not published.

The state counts and sequencing are not published.

The register widths and stage count are not published.

- **Counter (ROI coordinate counters within the 16,384 by 12,288 scope; zoom-factor select; dual-stream frame counter)** — The zoom window is cut from the full scope, so ROI coordinate counters track its position: the horizontal counter runs to 16,384, 14 bits wide (arithmetic — 2 to the 14th is 16,384 exactly), and the vertical counter runs to 12,288, also 14 bits wide (arithmetic — 2 to the 13th is 8,192, below 12,288, and 2 to the 14th is 16,384, the smallest power of two above it). The zoom-factor select steps between 2x and 4x, 1 bit wide (arithmetic), and a frame counter tracks the dual streams. No other counter width is claimed.

The shifter width is not published.

- **Synchronizer (AI engine clock domain vs ISP domain; full-stream vs zoom-stream synchronisation)** — The AI engine and the ISP do not share one clock, so synchronizers carry the frame into the AI engine's domain for tracking and the tracking result back again to the ROI selector, in the standard two-flop construction, and a second synchronizer keeps the full and zoomed streams on the same frame. The domain frequencies and synchronizer depths are not published.

- **Credit counter (bandwidth and compute budget shared by the two streams, the remosaic and the tracking inference)** — Two streams plus remosaic plus tracking inference share one AI engine and one memory path, so a credit counter budgets bandwidth and compute among them — holding back the zoomed stream when its credits are spent so the full view keeps recording, and the reverse — the mechanism behind the three-way contention the Level-2 bottleneck section names. The credit limits and the counter widths are not published, so no counter total is claimed. Standard construction.

**Parameter honesty.** Honesty: Samsung publishes no ISP block diagram and no per-stage latency for this feature either, so the primitives below are mapped from the documented functions in order of the Samsung Newsroom ISOCELL Zoom Anyplace and E2E AI Remosaic article, not from a die diagram. Samsung's published account pairs the tracking with the Qualcomm AI engine, and Samsung has not published a separate Exynos-side account of the feature, so the tracking primitives are mapped from the documented tracking function, not from an Exynos NPU diagram. Every published figure is already recorded at Level 2; no new chip-specific number is claimed here. The only new numbers are counter widths computed from published figures and labelled arithmetic. Generic constructions are labelled standard construction.
#### Down to the gates: Tetra2pixel remosaic and E2E AI Remosaic — the 200 MP stills path

Samsung publishes no gate-level structure for the Exynos 2400 ISP 200 MP stills path — no netlist, no standard-cell description, no transistor count for the Tetra2pixel binning, the remosaic, the E2E AI Remosaic parallelism, the Smart-ISO Pro plus DSG HDR merge, the Super QPD autofocus or the deep-learning fusion engine. The deepest published description is the Samsung Newsroom ISOCELL HP2 article of January 17, 2023, which documents the 200-million 0.6 micrometre pixels, Tetra2pixel binning to 1.2 micrometre 50 MP or 2.4 micrometre 12.5 MP, the D-VTG full-well capacity boost of more than 33 percent, DSG in 50 MP mode and the Smart-ISO Pro single-exposure HDR, together with the Samsung Newsroom ISOCELL Zoom Anyplace and E2E AI Remosaic article of October 31, 2023, which documents E2E running the remosaic and the ISP simultaneously and cutting the remosaic latency by up to half. What follows takes each Level-3 primitive down to gates and transistors using the primer's bottom layer — the universal gates, the latch and the flip-flop, the 6T SRAM cell, the CAM cell and the full adder — and every gate or transistor figure is the standard textbook construction of the named primitive, not a claim about Samsung's actual netlist. Where a primitive's geometry is not published, no total is claimed.

- **FIFO / queue (sensor readout staging; remosaic-to-ISP handoff queue; JPEG output queue)** — A FIFO at gate level is a storage array plus two pointer counters plus full/empty comparators: the storage is a register file of D flip-flops or a small SRAM bank, the write pointer and read pointer are counters of N flip-flops plus N full adders each, incrementing on push and pop, and the full and empty flags are comparators over the pointer values — one XOR per compared bit feeding an AND tree. The raw frame leaves the sensor for the ISP, so a readout FIFO stages the sensor stream while the remosaic works the previous frame, decoupling the sensor readout rate from the remosaic rate. E2E AI Remosaic runs the remosaic and the ISP simultaneously instead of in sequence, so a handoff queue sits between the two parallel stages, absorbing the rate mismatch while both run at once, and the finished frame waits in an output queue for the JPEG encoder. The queue depths and the readout width are not published, so the pointer widths — and therefore the counter and comparator totals — are not claimed. Standard construction.
- **SRAM bank / line buffers (Quad Bayer neighbourhood store for array conversion; 200 MP frame staging)** — The working store is an SRAM bank in the primer's form: rows of 6T SRAM cells — two cross-coupled inverters (4 transistors) plus two access transistors — behind a row decoder (a NAND-gate tree selecting one wordline), transmission-gate column muxes (2 transistors per leg) and latch-type differential sense amplifiers. Remosaic rebuilds full-colour pixels from groups of same-colour pixels in the Quad Bayer layout, so the conversion cannot work on one pixel alone — line buffers hold the neighbouring rows while the array conversion runs, and the frame itself is staged on chip while the parallel remosaic and ISP stages work it. A 200 MP frame carries 16,384 by 12,288 samples to convert, which is why this stage, not the sensor, sets the pace of the stills path. The line-buffer depth, banking, port counts and widths are not published, so no cell total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Multiplier array (remosaic interpolation weights; Smart-ISO Pro merge weighting)** — A multiplier array is partial-product generation plus an adder tree: each multiply generates partial products with AND gates — one AND gate per bit-pair — and reduces them through full adders, 28 transistors each in the standard-cell form, two half adders of XOR, AND and OR gates. Rebuilding a full-colour pixel from its same-colour neighbours is interpolation, and interpolation is multiply work: each neighbour is weighted before the sum, and Smart-ISO Pro merges different ISO readouts from a single exposure the same way, weighting each readout before the merge. Each is a multiplier array feeding an adder tree. The array dimensions, lane count and number format are not published, so no multiplier total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Adder tree (Tetra2pixel binning sums, 4-in-1 and 16-in-1; remosaic interpolation sums; Smart-ISO Pro merge sums)** — An adder tree is full adders arranged in a binary reduction: partial sums reduce one stage per halving of their count, each full adder two half adders — 2 XOR, 2 AND and 1 OR gates, about 28 transistors in a standard cell. Binning is addition: 4-in-1 binning sums four neighbouring pixels into one 50 MP pixel, 16-in-1 binning sums sixteen into one 12.5 MP pixel, and an adder tree collapses each group — the standard construction — while the remosaic interpolation and the Smart-ISO Pro merge sum their weighted values the same way. The tree depth and width are not published, so no adder total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Comparator (binning-mode selection thresholds; highlight clip and D-VTG full-well thresholds; Smart-ISO Pro ISO merge thresholds)** — A comparator is an XOR per compared bit feeding an AND tree for equality, or a subtractor of full adders whose sign bit decides magnitude: equal is all XOR outputs zero, greater-than is a priority chain over the most-significant differing bit. Choosing the binning mode is a comparison: bright light stays at full 200 MP, low light bins to 50 MP or 12.5 MP, and the light level is judged against thresholds. D-VTG adds a second transfer gate in each pixel, lifting full-well capacity by more than 33 percent, so highlights are judged against the raised full-well threshold before they wash out, and Smart-ISO Pro compares its ISO readouts to decide which contributes to each pixel. The comparator count, widths and threshold values are not published, so no comparator total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Priority encoder / arbiter (remosaic vs ISP memory-path arbitration — the E2E contention the Level-2 bottleneck names)** — A priority encoder is a tree of OR gates with a priority chain: N request lines reduce to a grant index naming the highest-priority active request, with a round-robin variant adding a rotating priority register of D flip-flops. E2E AI Remosaic runs the remosaic and the ISP at the same time, so the two stages contend for the same memory path while a 200 MP frame is in flight — the new bottleneck the Level-2 section names — and an arbiter decides which stage's access moves next when both are ready at once, with a priority encoder turning the winning request into the access index the memory controller sees. The arbitration policy is not published, so no further encoder total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Mux / demux (binning-mode select full vs 4-in-1 vs 16-in-1; remosaic vs bypass; stills vs video path select)** — A mux is a transmission-gate tree or a NAND/NOR tree: a 2:1 mux is 2 transistors per input leg as transmission gates, and an N:1 mux is N minus 1 2:1 muxes arranged as a tree in log2(N) stages, selected by a decoder. One pipeline serves three binning modes, so a mux selects full 200 MP, 4-in-1 50 MP or 16-in-1 12.5 MP output from the sensor — a 3:1 select, 2 2:1 muxes in 2 stages by arithmetic — a second mux steers the frame through the remosaic or past it, a 2:1 select, and a third steers the finished frame to the stills JPEG path or the 4K60 HDR video path that Smart-ISO Pro also serves, a 2:1 select. The mux widths and select encoding are not published, so no further mux total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **FSM / controller (stills-path sequencer; E2E parallel-stage synchronisation controller; binning-mode controller)** — A finite-state machine is state bits plus next-state logic plus output logic: the state bits are master-slave D flip-flops (about 20–28 transistors each) and the next-state and output logic is a NAND/NOR network driven by the current state and the inputs. The six documented functions run in order, so a controller sequences the stills path — binning, remosaic, ISP, HDR merge, fusion, JPEG — a second controller keeps the remosaic and the ISP running in parallel without one overtaking the other, and a binning-mode controller picks the Tetra2pixel mode from the light level. That sequencer is a state machine of this form. Its state counts and the sequencing are not published, so no state-bit total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Pipeline registers (between binning, remosaic, ISP, fusion and JPEG stages; E2E overlap registers)** — A pipeline register is one D flip-flop per bit — about 20–28 transistors each, two cross-coupled latch stages — latched between stages so the next stage can start while the current stage's result is held. Each stills stage hands its result to the next through pipeline registers, so binning, remosaic, ISP, fusion and JPEG can overlap on successive frames instead of running one frame end to end — and the E2E overlap registers are what let the remosaic and the ISP run simultaneously, the structure that cuts the remosaic latency by up to half. The register widths and the stage count are not published, so no register total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Counter (pixel counter to the 200 MP frame; binning-mode index; row and column counters)** — A counter is N D flip-flops plus N full adders in a ripple or look-ahead chain, incrementing on each clock, with a comparator resetting it at the terminal count. The stills path counts what it processes: the pixel counter runs across the 200 MP frame — 16,384 by 12,288 samples is 201,326,592 pixels (arithmetic), so the counter is 28 bits wide (arithmetic — 2 to the 27th is 134,217,728, below 201,326,592, and 2 to the 28th is 268,435,456, the smallest power of two above it), being 28 D flip-flops (560–784 transistors) plus 28 full adders (784 transistors) — the binning-mode index steps across the three Tetra2pixel modes, 2 bits wide (arithmetic — 2 to the 1st is 2, below 3, and 2 to the 2nd is 4), being 2 D flip-flops (40–56 transistors) plus 2 full adders (56 transistors) — and row and column counters track the frame position, 14 bits each (arithmetic — 2 to the 14th is 16,384, the column count, and 2 to the 13th is 8,192, below the 12,288 row count, so 14 bits covers both), being 14 D flip-flops (280–392 transistors) plus 14 full adders (392 transistors). All three widths are arithmetic derived from the published figures and labelled as such; the counter widths themselves are not published. Standard construction.
- **Barrel shifter (bit-depth scaling from remosaic output toward JPEG and ISP depth; DSG dual-conversion scaling)** — A barrel shifter is a mux tree: shifting an N-bit value by a variable amount takes log2(N) stages of 2:1 muxes, each mux a transmission-gate pair (2 transistors per leg) or a NAND/NOR tree. DSG applies two separate conversion values to the analog signal in 50 MP mode, and the remosaic output has to be scaled toward the depth the ISP and the JPEG encoder take, so a barrel shifter shifts each value by a variable amount in one step to scale the depth. The shifter width is not published, so no shifter total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Synchronizer (sensor clock domain vs ISP domain; NPU handoff for scene optimisation)** — A synchronizer is two D flip-flops in series — about 20–28 transistors each — the first sampling the incoming signal in the new clock domain and the second re-sampling it a cycle later so metastability resolves before the value is used; a multi-bit crossing is an asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers, the pointers changing one bit at a time so a sampled pointer is never more than one count stale. The sensor, the ISP and the NPU beside the ISP do not share one clock, so synchronizers carry the raw frame into the ISP's domain and the finished frame out again to the NPU for scene optimisation, in the standard two-flop construction. The domain frequencies and synchronizer depths are not published, so no synchronizer total is claimed. Standard construction.
- **Credit counter (memory-bandwidth budget shared by the parallel remosaic and ISP stages)** — A credit counter is a down-counter of D flip-flops and full adders with a comparator: it starts at the budget, decrements on each issued request and increments on each returned credit, and a comparator blocks new requests when the count reaches zero. The parallel stages now demand bandwidth at the same time, so a credit counter budgets the shared memory path between the remosaic and the ISP — holding back one stage when its credits are spent so the other keeps its share — the mechanism behind the contention the Level-2 bottleneck section names. The credit limits and the counter widths are not published, so no counter total is claimed. Standard construction.

Honesty: Samsung publishes the 200 MP stills path at function level only — Tetra2pixel binning, remosaic, E2E AI Remosaic parallelism, Smart-ISO Pro plus DSG HDR, Super QPD autofocus and the deep-learning fusion engine with hardware noise reduction (Level-2 and Level-3 fact records) — and no gate-level structure for any part of the stills path appears in any Samsung source. Everything below is the standard textbook construction of the named primitive, pointing at the primer's bottom layer; none of it is a claim about Samsung's actual netlist (new Level-4 fact record: unverifiable).

### Apple A17 Pro

**Added: 2026-11-22** (deepened to Level-2/3/4 standard: 2026-11-27)

**Specs (wiki card).** TSMC 3 nm · 19B transistors · hardware ray tracing

**What it is / why it matters.** First 3 nm phone SoC: new GPU with mesh shading and ray tracing, ProRes/USB3 controllers, and a 35-TOPS Neural Engine. A17 Pro shows the phone SoC absorbing console features — process leadership spent on graphics and media, not just CPU.

**Building blocks.** Six named pieces, and the connections between them are the design:
- **6-core CPU cluster** — 2 performance + 4 efficiency Arm cores — the control centre, deliberately not where this generation's transistor budget went
- **6-core GPU with ray-tracing accelerators** — Apple's first hardware ray tracing, plus mesh shading — console features entering a phone GPU, and the block this process node was spent on
- **16-core Neural Engine (35 TOPS)** — The fixed-function inference block on the SoC fabric, fed from shared memory
- **Media engine** — ProRes encode/decode, HEVC/H.264, and — new this generation — hardware AV1 decode
- **Secure Enclave** — The isolated security processor handling keys and biometrics for the whole SoC
- **LPDDR5 controller + USB 3** — One shared memory pool for every engine above; the first USB 3 controller (10 Gb/s) in an iPhone rides along

**The piece that makes it special.** Where the 3 nm budget went. A17 Pro's CPU is an iteration; its GPU (ray tracing), media engine (AV1 decode) and I/O are the leaps. The first 3 nm phone SoC is a case study in process leadership being spent on the blocks users can see — games, video, cameras — rather than benchmark cores.

**How work flows.** Work is scheduled per engine: Apps place tasks on CPU, GPU, ANE or media engine — all reading the same LPDDR5 pool. Heavy media bypasses the CPU: Video and ProRes work runs in the media engine while the CPU idles. Results stay in place: Frames pass between ISP, GPU and ANE by pointer, not by copy.

**Trade-off accepted.** Thermals and fixity. A phone chassis cannot sustain the peak the silicon can reach, memory configuration is fixed at purchase, and every engine's capability is frozen at tape-out.
